1) If Dim. O between two blend repairs is less than or equal to five times the depth of

depth of this blend, blend the shadowed area, tangentially from the bottom of the
blend and curve to the blade tip corner to (Radius R1 or Radius R2) minimum
possible value.

a) Make sure that the profile is continuous.

(1) Any amount of surface oxidation, pitting or corrosion marks on the stage 1, 2, 3 and 4 booster
vanes is permitted.
SUBTASK 72-21-03-220-001-F00

stage 1 booster vane assembly, unless you are given other instructions

SUBTASK 72-21-03-220-002-F00

TASK 72-00-00-200-803-F00.

SUBTASK 72-21-03-220-003-F00

(a) Not serviceable.
SUBTASK 72-21-03-220-004-F00
(6) Examine the tip of the vanes (Area D) for damage:
(a) Cracks and tears
1) Cracks and tears are not permitted.
2) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles or 15 flight hours is permitted; if the damage
is less than 0.127 inch (3.25 mm) in length radially and 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) in length
axially.
(b) Dents
1) All damage is permitted with these limits:
a) Not more than 25 percent in depth of the blade airfoil thickness.

EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
b) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles or 15 flight hours is permitted, if the
damage is more than the limits and less than 40 percent of the blade airfoil
thickness.
(c) Nicks and scratches in airfoil (not on the leading and trailing edges)
1) All damage is permitted with these limits:
a) Not more than 25 percent in depth of the blade airfoil thickness.
b) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles or 15 flight hours is permitted, if the
damage is more than the limits.
(d) Nicks and scratches on the leading and trailing edges
1) All damage is permitted with these limits:
a) Not more than 0.04 inch (1 mm) in depth (axially).
b) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles or 15 flight hours is permitted, if the
damage is more than the limits.
(e) Local distortion
1) All distortion is permitted with these limits:
a) The radially damaged dimension is more than six times the axially damaged
dimension.
b) The dimension is less than 0.08 inch (2 mm) axially.
c) The dimension is less than 0.47 inch (12 mm) radially.
(f) Missing pieces
1) Missing pieces are not permitted.
SUBTASK 72-21-03-220-005-F00
(7) Examine the leading edge and trailing edges of the vane (Area E) for damage:
(a) Cracks
1) Cracks are not permitted.
2) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles or 15 flight hours is permitted; if the damage
is less than 0.127 inch (3.25 mm) radially and 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) axially.
(b) Tears
1) Tears are not permitted.
2) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles or 15 flight hours is permitted if the damage
is less than 0.127 inch (3.25 mm) radially and 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) axially.
(c) Dents
1) Dents are permitted with these limits:
a) Not more than 0.08 inch (2 mm) in depth axially.
2) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles or 15 flight hours is permitted before repair
or replacement of the vane, if the damage is more than the limits.
3) If the damage is more than the limits, repair the vane assembly leading edge.
a) Do this task, Repair the Stage 1 Booster Vane Assembly,
TASK 72-21-03-300-801-F00.
(d) Nicks and scratches
1) Nicks and scratches are permitted with these limits:

 ALL
a) Not more than 0.08 inch (2 mm) in depth (axially).
2) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles or 15 flight hours is permitted before repair

3) If the damage is more than the limits, repair the vane assembly leading edge.
a) Do this task, Repair the Stage 1 Booster Vane Assembly,
TASK 72-21-03-300-801-F00.
(e) Local distortion
1) All local distortion is permitted with these limits
a) The damaged dimension L is more than six times the maximum damaged
dimension X along the chord.
b) The maximum dimension X along the chord is less than 0.12 inch (3 mm).
c) The dimension L is less than 0.71 inch (18 mm).
2) A Continue-In-Service limit of 50 cycles or 75 flight hours is permitted, if the damage
is more than the limits.
(f) Erosion and deposits
1) All erosion and deposits are permitted.

1) Cracks and tears are not permitted.

is less than 0.127 inch (3.25 mm) radially and 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) axially.
(b) Dents
1) Dents are permitted with these limits:
a) Not more than 40 percent in depth of the blade airfoil thickness.
b) A Continue-In-Service limit of 50 cycles or 75 flight hours is permitted, if the

(c) Nicks and scratches
1) Nicks and scratches are permitted with these limits:
a) Not more than 40 percent in depth of the blade airfoil thickness.
(d) Local distortion
1) All local distortion is permitted with these limits:
a) The radially damaged dimension is more than six times the axially damaged

b) The dimension is less than 0.12 inch (3 mm) axially.
c) The dimension is less than 0.71 inch (18 mm) radially.
2) A Continue-In-Service limit of 50 cycles or 75 flight hours is permitted, if the damage

(a) Cracks

1) Unbonding or flaking is permitted with these limits

a) All dents on the forward edge and aft edge are permitted.

(a) To do this inspection, remove the stage 1 booster vane assembly from the power plant

1) Cracks are not permitted.

(d) Booster blade tip rubbing on the abradable coating
1) No limit for rubbing on the full circumference.

1) All pitting, nicks, dents or local distortion on the abradable coating is permitted.

2. Outlet Guide Vanes Removal
(Figure 401)
A. General
(1) The OGVs are found between the fan blades and the fan frame struts, in the secondary air
flow.
(2) There are 76 OGVs on each engine.
(3) In this procedure the outlet guide vanes will be referred to as the OGVs.

Reference Title

DEACTIVATION OF THE LEADING EDGE AND THE THRUST REVERSERS
(FOR GROUND MAINTENANCE), AND OPEN THE FAN COWL PANELS. IF
YOU DO NOT OBEY THE ABOVE SEQUENCE, INJURIES TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(1) Do this task: Open the Thrust Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-801-F00.
E. Outlet Guide Vanes Removal
SUBTASK 72-23-01-020-001-F00
(1) Do these steps to disconnect the OGV from the fan inlet:
(a) Remove the two bolts [1].
NOTE: Be prepared to catch each cup washer.
(b) Remove the two cup washers [2].

 ALL

platform from the inner shroud recess.

(4) Remove the OGV [3] from the power plant.
SUBTASK 72-23-01-210-001-F00

E. Outlet Guide Vanes Installation
SUBTASK 72-23-01-320-001-F00
(1) Do these steps to install the OGV seals [4]:
(a) Align the round cut of the two seals with the 4 o'clock hole of the inner OGV shroud
(borescope port).
1) If you install a new OGV seal, drill the borescope hole at the 4 o'clock position to a
diameter of 0.41 in. (10.4 mm).
(b) Align the round cut of the two seals with the 6 o'clock hole of the inner OGV shroud
(draining hole).
1) If you install a new OGV seal, drill the borescope hole at the 6 o'clock position to a
diameter of 0.16 in. (4 mm)
(c) Install the remaining 72 seals [4] in their related slots on the inner OGV shroud.

CAUTION

TRAILING EDGES DURING INSTALLATION.
(a) Carefully engage the OGV inner platform into the seal on the inner shroud.
(b) Move the OGV outer platform to the rear.
(c) Set the outward platform in the correct position on the fan case.

EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 72-23-01-420-002-F00
CAUTION
AREA AROUND ATTACHMENT HOLES MUST BE CLEAN AND DRY

(3) Do these steps to attach the OGV to the fan inlet:
(a) Install the two bolts [1] and the two cup washers [2].
(b) Tighten the bolts to 126.35 in-lb (14.28 N·m) - 139.65 in-lb (15.78 N·m).
(c) Remove all unwanted grease with a dry clean cloth.

D. Do a Check of the OGV's
SUBTASK 72-23-01-210-002-F00
(1) If you find damage that is not in the limits, replace the OGV, unless you are given other
instructions.
These are the tasks:
Outlet Guide Vanes Removal, TASK 72-23-01-000-801-F00,
Outlet Guide Vanes Installation, TASK 72-23-01-400-801-F00.
SUBTASK 72-23-01-210-003-F00
(2) Examine the OGV's for damage:
(a) Broken or missing vane
1) Not serviceable.
(b) Cracks and tears in the OGV vane
1) Not serviceable.
(c) Missing paint or coating
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) All missing paint and anodized coating is permitted.
(d) Nicks or dents on the leading or the trailing edges
1) Nicks and dents are permitted if the damage is less than 0.04 inch (1.0 millimeter) in
depth.
a) There is no limit to the number of nicks or dents.
2) If you find that the damage is more than 0.04 inch (1.0 millimeter) in depth.
a) There is no limit to the number of nicks or dents.
b) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles or 25 flight hours is permitted (use the
first limit to occur).
(e) Nicks or dents on the concave and (or) convex surfaces
1) There is no limit to the number of dents or nicks if the damage is smooth and less
than half of the vane thickness in depth.
a) There is no damage permitted on the two sides of the vane.
2) There is no limit to the number of nicks or dents if the damage is more than half of
the vane thickness, with this condition.
a) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles or 25 flight hours is permitted (use the
first limit to occur).
(f) Distortion of the leading or trailing edges
1) Distortion is permitted with these limits:
a) The axial depth is less than 0.1 inch (2.5 millimeter).
b) The radial length is less than 1.0 inch (25 mm).

(3) Examine the damage to the seals that mate with the OGV surfaces.
(a) Cracks, cuts or tears on the mating surface of the seal with the OGV shroud.
1) Not serviceable.

(b) Cracks, cuts or tears that are not on the mating surface of the seal.

3. 12 O'clock Engine Strut Inspection
A. General
(1) The 12 o'clock engine strut can be found at the thrust reverser extension ring.
(2) Contact with the thrust reverser insulation blanket can damage the 12 o'clock engine strut.
B. References
Reference Title

WARNING

THE THRUST REVERSER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THIS INSTRUCTION,
INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(1) Do this task: Open the Thrust Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-801-F00.
F. Procedure
SUBTASK 72-23-03-211-001-F01
(1) Look for signs of wear and gouges on the 12 o'clock engine strut.
(a) If the damage is 0.010 in. (0.254 mm) or less in depth, do this blend repair:
1) Use a light abrasive mat, G00251 or emory cloth and blend out the gouges.
2) Use a 20:1 length-to-depth ratio for smooth transition.
3) Blend no deeper than the depth of the gouges.
4) Maintain a 125RA or better surface finish.
(b) If the damage is 0.011 in. (0.279 mm)-0.020 in. (0.508 mm) in depth, do these steps:
1) Do the above blend repair.
2) The 12 o'clock strut can remain in service for up to 60 months.
a) When this period is up, replace the 12 o'clock strut.
(c) If the damage is 0.021 in. (0.533 mm)-0.030 in. (0.762 mm) in depth, do these steps:
1) Do the above blend repair.
2) The 12 o'clock strut can remain in service for up to 24 months.
a) When this period is up, replace the 12 o'clock strut.
(d) If the damage is more than 0.030 in. (0.762 mm) in depth, there is no on-wing repair:
1) Replace the 12 o'clock strut within 10 days.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

(2) Make sure the attach bolts and lockwire for each of the thrust mounts is not missing or loose:
NOTE: You should use a flashlight and an inspection mirror to examine the bolts that are not
easy to see.
CAUTION
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU INSTALL PARTS THAT ARE AROUND AN
OPEN VBV DOOR. PARTS THAT FALL INTO AN OPEN VBV DOOR CAN
FALL IN THE HIGH PRESSURE COMPRESSOR OF THE ENGINE. PARTS
WHICH FALL INTO THE ENGINE CAN CAUSE ENGINE DAMAGE AT THE
FIRST ENGINE RUN.
(a) Missing or broken bolt
1) Use a flashlight to shine thru the nut where the bolt is missing:
NOTE: The nuts are in the VBV cavity in the fan frame.
a) Make sure that a piece of broken bolt is not in the nut.
2) If no piece of bolt [3] stays in the nut [4], do these steps:
a) Lubricate the threads of a replacement bolt with graphite mineral vaseline,
D00601 [CP2101].
b) Install the bolt [3].
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
c) Tighten the bolt [3] to 547-603 pound-inches (62-68 Newton meters).
d) Examine the other bolts [3] for missing or damaged lockwire.
e) Install new safety wire, G02345 [CP8001] or safety cable, G50065 [CP8006]
[2] to the bolts [3] in groups of two.
3) If a piece of bolt [3] stays in the nut, do these steps:
CAUTION
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU INSTALL PARTS THAT ARE AROUND
AN OPEN VBV DOOR. PARTS THAT FALL INTO AN OPEN VBV
DOOR CAN FALL IN THE HIGH PRESSURE COMPRESSOR OF
THE ENGINE. PARTS WHICH FALL INTO THE ENGINE CAN
CAUSE ENGINE DAMAGE AT THE FIRST ENGINE RUN.
a) Make sure that the VBV doors are in the closed position.
b) If the VBV doors are not fully closed, do this task: VBV Actuation System -
Manual Operation, TASK 75-32-00-730-801-F00
c) Remove the applicable fan duct panel, do this task: Fan Duct Panel Removal,
TASK 72-23-07-000-801-F00.
d) Remove the two bolts [5].
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THE NUT DOES NOT FALL AND REMAIN IN THE
VBV CAVITY. WHEN THE BRACKET IS REMOVED, THE NUT IS
NOT HELD ON THE FAN FRAME AND COULD FALL INTO THE
ENGINE.
e) Remove the bracket [6] and nut [4].
f) Install a new nut [4].
g) Install the bracket [6].
h) Lubricate the threads of the two bolts [5] with Dow Corning 321 lubricant,
D00641 [CP5062].
i) Install and tighten the two bolts [5] with your hand.
NOTE: This is to hold the bracket [6].
j) Make sure that the nut [4] can move freely axially.
k) Tighten the two bolts [5] to 110-120 pound-inches (12.4-13.6 Newton meters).
l) Lubricate the threads of a new bolt [3] with graphite mineral vaseline, D00601
[CP2101].
m) Install the bolt [3].
n) Tighten the bolt [3] to 547-603 pound-inches (62-68 Newton meters).
o) Install safety wire, G02345 [CP8001] or safety cable, G50065 [CP8006] [2] to
the bolts [3] in groups of two.
(b) Missing or damaged lockwire
1) Remove all damaged pieces of lockwire.
2) Tighten the bolts [3] to 547-603 pound-inches (62-68 Newton meters).
3) Install new safety wire, G02345 [CP8001] or safety cable, G50065 [CP8006] to the
bolts [3] in groups of two.

 ALL

SUBTASK 72-23-05-210-001-F00
(4) Do a check of the fan frame:
(a) Cracks in the fan frame case, except between fan frame struts 7 and 8.
1) Cracks are not permitted.
2) Missing material is not permitted.
NOTE: There is no service extension permitted for all cracks or missing material
found.
(b) Cracks in the fan frame shroud located at the forward acoustical panel attachment
(between fan frame struts 7 and 8).
NOTE: It is necessary to remove the acoustical panel before you do this procedure. If
corrosion under the anchor nut is observed during removal of the acoustical
panel, do the Corrosion under anchor nuts procedure below.
1) One single crack per forward acoustical panel attachment is permitted with these
conditions:
a) It is not more than 5.0 in. (127.0 mm) in length.
b) There is a minimum separation of 4.0 in. (101.6 mm) from other cracks.
c) You make sure that all cracks are inside the Nondestructive Test (NDT)
inspection area (Figure 604).
d) A crack must have two or more legs and must have the same source of each
leg from the same rivet or hole.
NOTE: One leg cannot divide from another leg.
e) You do the stop drill procedure to stop the crack
(TASK 72-23-05-300-801-F00).
f) A continue-in-service limit of 10 cycles or 15 hours is permitted, if you find
cracks that are more than the above serviceable limits:
<1> 10-flight cycle deferral is permitted, contact your CFM International
(CFMI) Support Center for disposition.
<2> To use this 10-flight cycle deferral, you must put a bead of sealant,
A50096, on the outer surface of the crack (TASK 51-31-00-390-804).

2) Cracks that go in all directions are not permitted.
(c) Dents or nicks on the struts
1) All dents or nicks are permitted with these limits:
a) It is not more than 0.08 in. (2.0 mm) in depth.
b) A continue-in-service limit of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted, if you find
dents or nicks that are more than the limit.
(d) Fretting wear on V-groove outer ring (Figure 601)
1) All quantities of fretting/wear and missing varnish PTFE (Polytetraflouroethylene
(Teflon)) or sulfuric anodization coating on V-groove and sealing surface is
permitted.
(e) Distortion on the aft lip (Figure 601 (Sheet 2))
1) Distortion on the aft lip is permitted with these conditions:
a) It is not more than 0.180 in. (4.57 mm) in width.
b) It is not more than 0.094 in. (2.4 mm) in depth.
c) It is not more than 1.496 in. (38.0 mm) in length.
d) There is only one area that has the distortion.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) If the distortion is not in the permitted limits, do this task: Fan Frame Shroud Aft Lip
Cold Reforming Repairs, TASK 72-23-05-350-801-F00.
(f) Nicks, dents or impacts on the aft lip
1) Nicks, dents or impacts on the aft lip are not permitted.
2) If nicks, dents or impacts are found, do this task: Fan Frame Aft Lip Blend Area
Repairs, TASK 72-23-05-300-803-F00.
(g) Elongated holes on the fan frame flanges
1) All elongated holes for single or double bracket configuration are permitted with
these conditions:
a) The hole is not more than 0.279 in. (7.1 mm) in width.
b) The hole is not more than 0.31 in. (7.9 mm) in length (unidirectional wear).
c) The hole is not more than 0.019 in. (0.5 mm) in depth.
d) Install again the applicable bracket with the new bolts, washers and nuts after
the initial installation procedure.
2) All elongated holes with double bracket (on each side of flange) are permitted with
these conditions:
a) The hole is not more than 0.279 in. (7.1 mm) in width.
b) The hole is not more than 0.433 in. (11.0 mm) in length (unidirectional wear).
c) The hole is not more than 0.039 in. (1.0 mm) in depth.
d) Install again the applicable new bracket with the new bolts, washers and nuts
after the initial installation procedure.
e) A continue-in-service limit of 250 cycles is permitted to replace the bracket.
(h) Corrosion under anchor nuts
1) Corrosion is not permitted, remove the corrosion under the anchor nuts of the fan
frame shroud. Refer to TASK 72-23-05-300-805-F00 or
TASK 72-23-05-300-811-F00 or TASK 72-23-05-300-807-F00.
NOTE: The TASK 72-23-05-300-805-F00 and TASK 72-23-05-300-811-F00 can
only be performed, if within limits of the repair.
NOTE: The TASK 72-23-05-300-807-F00 has to be done to remove the corrosion
on acoustic panel bolt holes only.
NOTE: The TASK 72-23-05-300-807-F00 can only be performed, if one of these
conditions is met:
- Corrosion is limited to the hole in a 0.4449 in. (11.3 mm) diameter area
centered on the holes.
- Corrosion is 0.0394 in. (1.0 mm) deep in an 1.4567 in. (37.0 mm) area
centered on the holes with a remaining wall thickness more than 0.157 in.
(4.0 mm) for section A-A, or more than 0.165 in. (4.2 mm) for section E-E.
Refer Figure 606.
NOTE: This task is applicable with restrictions in the area between the struts 7 and
8 (Integrated Drive Generator (IDG) Air/Oil cooler) on the fan frame shroud
POST SB 72-0495.
a) A continue-in-service of 50 cycles is permitted to remove the corrosion, if no
crack is found during the General Visual Inspection of the corroded area.

(TASK 70-40-01-230-801-F00):
a) Sensitivity level 3.
b) Indications more than 0.0118 in. (0.30 mm) are not permitted.
c) Linear indications are not permitted.

7. Fan Frame Shroud (Removal of the Corrosion in Acoustic Panels Bolt Holes by Bushing and/or
Washer Installation) Repairs
(Figure 815, Figure 816,Figure 817, Figure 818, Figure 819, and Figure 820)
A. General
(1) This repair task gives instructions to remove the corrosion in or around acoustic panels bolt
holes, as follows (Figure 815):
NOTE: This repair must be done only in the acoustic panels bolt holes or on the outer skin of
the fan frame shroud. The removal of corrosion cannot be done on a flange or a
radius. Bushing or washer installation is not permitted if there is an interaction with B6,
B7 and/or B8 flange radius of the fan frame shroud.
NOTE: This repair is subject to restrictions for “Type B” P/N (with doubler between strut 7 and
strut 8). Refer to the area with restrictions on the Figure 815.
NOTE: This repair can be applied only if access is possible.
(a) Bushing installation only, if corrosion is limited to the hole.
(b) Washer installation only, if corrosion is limited to the outer skin.
(c) Bushing and washer installation, if corrosion extends from the hole.
NOTE: If you need to apply paragraph 7.A.(1)(c), there are three different procedures:
• washer installation after bushing installation (Procedure 1)
• bushing installation after washer installation (Procedure 2)
• bushing and washer installation at the same time (Procedure 3).

(e) Remove the puller from the drive shaft housing [2].
(f) Remove the inner radial drive shaft [5] from the splines of the radial IGB bevel gear.
(g) Remove and discard the O-ring [4].

E. Procedure
SUBTASK 72-23-06-900-001-F00
(1) If you find damage that is not in the limits, replace the inner radial drive shaft, unless you are
given other instructions.
SUBTASK 72-23-06-220-001-F00
(2) Do a check of the inner radial drive shaft:
(a) Nicks and dents
1) All damage is permitted with these limits:
a) Not more than 0.025 inch (0.64 mm) in depth after you remove the high metal.
Refer to General Removal of High Metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance
Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00).
(b) Scratches
1) All damage is permitted with these limits:
a) You cannot feel the scratch with a 0.03 inch (0.76 mm) radius scriber.
(c) Cracks
1) Not permitted.
(d) Lack of protective material on non-machined surfaces
1) All damage is permitted with these limits:
a) There is not more than 5 percent of the total surface area that does not have
protective material.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(e) Corrosion
1) Not permitted.
(f) Wear
1) Not permitted.

WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENTS OF THE OIL SYSTEM IF THE ENGINE
IS HOT. THESE COMPONENTS STAY HOTTER THAN OTHER
COMPONENTS. HOT COMPONENTS CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT OPEN THE OIL SYSTEM UNTIL THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO.
THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES AFTER AN
ENGINE STOPS. A PRESSURIZED OIL SYSTEM CAN RELEASE A SPRAY OF
HOT OIL THAT CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON YOU. AFTER FIVE MINUTES WHEN THE APU
STOPS, LET THE OIL SYSTEM PRESSURE GO TO ZERO. PUT ON
PROTECTIVE CLOTHES, GOGGLES AND EQUIPMENT, OR LET THE APU
BECOME COOL. IF YOU REMOVE THE OIL FILLER CAP WITH THE OIL
SYSTEM PRESSURIZED, A SPRAY OF HOT OIL CAN BURN YOU.
CAUTION
DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON THE ENGINE OR OTHER COMPONENTS.
IMMEDIATELY CLEAN THE COMPONENT IF OIL FALLS ON IT. OIL CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO PAINT AND RUBBER.

(c) Nicks, dents, and scratches on the fan inlet case (Figure 603).
NOTE: The trinomial inspection is the quickest method but gives you less margin in
terms of limits. The template inspection takes more time but gives larger limits.
NOTE: For areas 4, 5 and 6 post CFM56-7B-SB 72-0553, the following inspections are
applicable after removal of a 13.937 in. (354 mm) radius anti-erosion paint
around the nick, dent or scratch to check if other ones are present below
anti-erosion paint.
NOTE: One of the three following inspections shall be used for inspection of nicks, dents
and scratches of the inner and outer skin of the fan inlet case.
NOTE: Inspection of FWD and AFT zones (FWD zone: Areas 1 and 2, AFT zone: Areas
4, 5, and 6) shall be carried using only one inspection method. Each zone can be
controlled with a different method. Area 3 can only be inspected per Inspection 2.
• Inspection 1 is the simplest inspection method that does not take into account
indications with a depth of 0.004 in. (0.1 mm) or less (only applicable for Areas
1 and 2). For Post SB 72–0931 parts, we recommend that you use Inspection 2
which is more permissive.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
• Inspection 2 is the most common trinomial inspection method and takes into
account all nicks, dents and scratches, whatever their depth (applicable for all
Areas).
• Inspection 3 is the most efficient inspection method and provides the biggest
range of indication allowance (only applicable for Areas 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6).
NOTE: Among Inspections 1, 2 and 3, if one inspection or more pass, the fan inlet case
is serviceable.
1) Alternative procedure available - Simplified Criteria for Areas 1 and 2 only.
NOTE: Indications with a depth of 0.004 in. (0.1 mm) or less are not taken into
account and are considered as acceptable whatever the distance with other
indications.
NOTE: Take into account the distance between two indications all around the area
without area restriction.
Example: If the indication one [Depth = 0.010 in. (0.25 mm); Length =
0.90 in. (22.86 mm)] is in Area 1 at 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) from Area 2, then no
indication is permitted in Areas 1 and 2 if the distance is less than 3.0 in.
(76.2 mm).
NOTE: Two opposite indications or repairs on outer and inner skin are not
permitted.

72-24-01-220-801-F00Fan Inlet Case Template InspectionPDF p. 881
4. Fan Inlet Case Template Inspection
A. General
(1) This task gives instructions to perform a template inspection of the containment case.
(2) The template inspection is an alternative procedure to examine nicks, dents, and scratches for
Areas 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6.
(3) This task finds the most impacted area.
(a) This area is delimited by a template.
(b) The control area takes into account indications of the inner and outer skins.
(c) Examine all combinations and turn the mask in many directions.
1) A combination is given by the depth and length of the indications on the inner and
outer skins in the template.
(d) Measure the length and depth of each indication.
1) Record these parameters in a table to find the severity of each indication.
(e) The sum of the severities gives the serviceable limits of the containment case.

F. Fan Inlet Case Template Inspection
SUBTASK 72-24-01-220-001-F00
(1) Remove the high metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00).
SUBTASK 72-24-01-220-007-F00
(2) Do a local swab etching before you examine the fan inlet case by Fluorescent Penetrant
Inspection (FPI) (TASK 70-10-11-800-801-F00).
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 72-24-01-220-008-F00
(3) Do a FPI of the suspected areas (TASK 70-40-01-230-801-F00).
SUBTASK 72-24-01-220-009-F00
(4) Examine the fan inlet case for nicks, dents, and scratches (Figure 615).
(a) The template inspection is a 360-degree inspection.
1) Consider Areas 1 and 2, and Areas 4, 5, and 6 as one area to put the template on it.
2) Don't take into account the border between Areas 1 and 2, and Areas 4, 5, and 6.
(b) All the possible combinations must be considered (Figure 610 and Figure 611).
1) The combination with the worst severity is the one that gives the serviceability
status of the fan containment case.
SUBTASK 72-24-01-220-002-F00
(5) Identify all the indications (nicks, dents, scratches) on the inner and outer skins that are more
than 0.004 in. (0.1 mm) in depth.
SUBTASK 72-24-01-211-001-F00
(6) Identify the worst combination and try all the possible template positions (Figure 610 and
Figure 611).
SUBTASK 72-24-01-970-001-F00
(7) For each combination, record the depth and length of the indications that are more than
0.004 in. (0.1 mm) in depth in the table (Figure 616).
(a) If an indication is not fully in the template, include the full length of the indication even if
that part extends out of the template.
SUBTASK 72-24-01-970-004-F00
(8) For Areas 1 and 2 only, record the minimum distance from A1 flange and the maximum
distance from A1 flange to use the multiplying factor to decrease the severity of each indication
(Figure 612, Figure 613, and Figure 614).
(a) Make sure that for Areas 1 and 2 there are less than 10 indications with a depth of
0.004 in. (0.102 mm) or less in the template.
NOTE: If an indication cannot be measured because it is too small, do not take it into
account.
(b) If such a combination is possible, this inspection procedure cannot be used.
SUBTASK 72-24-01-970-002-F00
(9) Define the severity of each indication with the example chart (Figure 617).
(a) Go out to the indication depth up to the length indication curve (Step A, Figure 617).
(b) Come back to the severity axis (Step B, Figure 617).
(c) Use the applicable chart to determine each severity (Figure 619 and Figure 620).
(d) Record the severity value in the table (Figure 614).
1) Use the table for combination 1 as an example (Figure 616).
(e) Find the multiplying factor for each indication for Areas 1 and 2 only, as follows
(Figure 613):
1) To find the multiplying factor for the minimum distance from the A1 flange and
maximum distance from the A1 flange, do these steps:
a) Project the distance from the A1 flange on the horizontal axis to the curve.
b) Project the distance from A1 flange on the curve to the vertical axis.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
c) Get value for the minimum distance from A1 flange.
d) Get value for the maximum distance from A1 flange.
e) Take into account only the highest multiplying factor for each indication.
2) Find the special severity of each indication on Areas 1 and 2.
a) Multiply the multiplying factor by the severity value.
3) Record this specific severity for Areas 1 and 2.
4) Do these steps for each combination.
(f) If it is necessary, use the following steps as an example of calculation (Figure 618):
1) Indications 1 and 2 in Figure 612 are located in the same combination and are as
follows:
• Indication number 1: 24%
• Indication number 2: 60%
• Indication number 3: 20%.
2) Sum of these severities without the special severities is 104% > 100%.
a) The indications without the special severities isn't serviceable.
3) Take into account the distance of each indication from the A1 flange (Figure 612
and Figure 613).
4) Values for indications are, as follows:
• Indication number 1: minimum distance is 1.4 in. (36 mm) and maximum distance
is 1.73 in. (44 mm)
• Indication number 2: minimum distance is 3.46 in. (88 mm) and maximum
distance is 3.77 in. (96 mm)
• Indication number 3: minimum distance is 2.2 in. (56 mm) and maximum distance
is 2.36 in. (60 mm).
5) Make a plot of these values on the multiplying factor curve (Figure 613).
6) Multiply the severities that you calculated before the multiplying factor:
• Indication number 1: MAX [0.36 and 0.42] => 0.42
• Indication number 2: MAX [0.60 and 0.72] => 0.72
• Indication number 3: MAX [0.78 and 0.98] => 0.98.
7) The corrected severities are, as follows:
• Indication number 1: 24% x 0.42 = 10.08%
• Indication number 2: 60% x 0.72 = 43.20%
• Indication number 3: 20% x 0.98 = 19.60%.
8) The sum of the special severities is 72.88%.
9) The indications are permitted with the correct severities.
SUBTASK 72-24-01-970-003-F00
(10) For addition of all the severities, do these steps:
(a) For a given combination add the special severities for the indications on Areas 1 and 2,
and the severities for indications on Areas 4, 5, and 6.
1) Record the sum in the table (Figure 614).
2) The most impacted area is delimited by the template (Figure 621).
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) For Areas 1 and 2:
<1> Dimension A - 2.79 in. (70.87 mm)
<2> Dimension B - 0.79 in. (20.07 mm).
b) For Areas 4, 5, and 6:
<1> Dimension A - 9.84 in. (249.94 mm)
<2> Dimension B - 9.84 in. (249.94 mm).
(b) If the combination of all the severities is less than or equal to 100 percent, the indications
on the fan case are serviceable.
SUBTASK 72-24-01-390-002-F00
(11) Do a spot touch-up of the oxide film coating on the inspected areas
(TASK 70-10-04-380-801-F00).

F. Examine the Abradable Shroud
SUBTASK 72-24-02-210-001-F00
(1) Do a visual check of the abradable shroud for damage:
(a) If findings are more than these limits, do this task: Recondition of the Abradable Shroud,
TASK 72-24-02-200-802-F00, unless you are given other instructions.
(b) Cracks.
1) There is no limit to the number of cracks.
(c) Craters (length < 5 X width) and impacts other than cracks, grooves, circumferential
impacts, disbonding or rub marks.
1) All craters and impacts (other than cracks, grooves, circumferential impacts,
disbonding or rub marks) are permitted with these limits:
a) The total of all impacted areas is not more than 160 in2
(1032 cm2
).
b) Each impacted area is not more than 30 in2
(194 cm2
).
c) Each impacted area is not more than 2.5 in. (63.5 mm) in axial width.
d) The minimum distance between impacted areas is equal to the maximum
width of the nearest single impacted area.
e) The fan case parent metal does not show through.
2) If the fan case parent metal shows through, a Continue-In-Service limit of 50 flight
cycles or 75 flight hours (whichever occurs first) is permitted if:
a) Craters and impacts are within dimensional limits.
b) There is no finding on the parent metal under visual check.
3) If the fan case parent metal shows through, protect the back of the affected area.
a) Do this task: Spot Touch-Up of Oxide Film Coating on Aluminum Alloys for
Protection, TASK 70-10-04-380-801-F00.
4) If the service extension limits are expired, do this task: Recondition of the Abradable
Shroud, TASK 72-24-02-200-802-F00.
(d) Grooves (length > 5 X width and pointed within 0-80 degrees the engine axis).
1) All grooves are permitted with these limits:
a) The maximum width of one groove is not more than 0.32 in. (8 mm).
b) The total groove width is not more than 1.25 in. (32 mm) with a separation of
not less than 0.1 in. (2.5 mm).
c) The fan case parent metal does not show through.
2) If the fan case parent metal shows through, a Continue-In-Service limit of 50 flight
cycles or 75 flight hours (whichever occurs first) is permitted if:
a) Grooves are within dimensional limits.
b) There is no finding on the parent metal under visual check.

3) If the fan case parent metal shows through, protect the back of the affected area.
a) Do this task: Spot Touch-Up of Oxide Film Coating on Aluminum Alloys for
Protection, TASK 70-10-04-380-801-F00.
4) If the service extension limits are expired, do this task: Recondition of the Abradable
Shroud, TASK 72-24-02-200-802-F00.
(e) Circumferential impact (360 degrees or pointed within 80-90 degrees the engine axis)
1) All circumferential impacts are permitted with these limits:
a) The maximum width of one or cumulative impact is not more than 1.5 in.
(38.1 mm).
b) The fan case parent metal does not show through.
2) If the maximum axial width of one or cumulative impact is not more than 2 in.
(51 mm), a Continue-In-Service limit of 50 flight cycles or 75 flight hours (whichever
occurs first) is permitted if:
a) The parent metal does not show through.
3) If the fan case parent metal shows through, a Continue-In-Service limit of 50 flight
cycles or 75 flight hours (whichever occurs first) is permitted if:
a) The circumferential impacts are within dimensional limits.
b) There is no finding on the parent metal under visual check.
4) If the fan case parent metal shows through, protect the back of the affected area.
a) Do this task: Spot Touch-Up of Oxide Film Coating on Aluminum Alloys for
Protection, TASK 70-10-04-380-801-F00.
5) If the service extension limits are expired, do this task: Recondition of the Abradable
Shroud, TASK 72-24-02-200-802-F00.
(f) Disbonding (other than cracks, craters, grooves, circumferential impacts or rub marks),
the fan case parent metal shows through.
1) A Continue-In-Service limit of 50 flight cycles or 75 flight hours (whichever occurs
first) is permitted if:
a) The cumulative of all impacted areas (including craters (length < 5 X width)
and impacts other than cracks, grooves, circumferential impacts or rub marks)
is not more than 160 in2
(1032 cm2
).
b) Each impacted area is not more than 30 in2
(194 cm2
).
c) Each impacted area is not more than 2.5 in. (63.5 mm) in axial width.
d) The minimum distance between impacted areas is equal to the width of the
nearest single impacted area.
e) There is no finding on the parent metal under visual check.
2) If the fan case parent metal shows through, protect the back of the affected area.
a) Do this task: Spot Touch-Up of Oxide Film Coating on Aluminum Alloys for
Protection, TASK 70-10-04-380-801-F00.
3) Check every 10 flight cycles or 15 flight hours (whichever occurs first) that the
above conditions are still fulfilled.
4) If the service extension limits are expired, do this task: Recondition of the Abradable
Shroud, TASK 72-24-02-200-802-F00.
(g) Rear side strip erosion.

<b> "A" is the value read on the dial indicator.
<c> "B" is the value read on the dial indicator.

<f> If "C" is negative, subtract this value from "R".

NOTE: If the thin abradable layer does not bond to the case, remove and
apply the thin abradable layer again.
c) Apply the abradable in the reconditioning area.
NOTE: If necessary, apply the abradable in multiple layers.
d) Make sure that there is no lack of abradable at the interface between the
radius of the abradable liner and the case.
NOTE: Do not change the direction of abradable application.
(c) Scraping of the abradable material (Figure 811).
NOTE: The scraping tool and roller set is in upper position.
1) Put the scraping support in lower position with the two knurled buttons.
2) Put the scraping blade in position before the abradable to be reconditioned.
NOTE: Scraping is done in clockwise direction.
3) Disengage the lift lever from its position to lower the scraping tool and roller set
(Figure 809).
NOTE: The scraping support touches the containment case with its two rollers.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
THE SPEED OF OPERATION MUST BE SUFFICIENTLY SLOW NOT
TO PULL THE ABRADABLE MATERIAL AWAY AND CREATE HOLES.
4) Start scraping by turning the wheel to slowly rotate the tool.
a) Regularly, remove abradable material from the scraping blade.
5) Repair areas with air bubbles by piercing them and adding abradable material.
6) Put the scraping support in upper position with the two knurled buttons.
7) Put the scraping tool and roller set in upper position with the lift lever (Figure 809).
8) Quickly remove the abradable material from the scraping blade with acetone
solvent, B01058 [CP1039].
(d) Put the polyester film in position on the rolls.
1) Unwind the polyester film and put it under the three rolls. Keep the polyester film
tensioned against the four rolls.
a) Attach the polyester film to the scraping support with 3M 471 tape, G51486
[CP2109].
NOTE: Make sure that the polyester film is kept tensioned.
(e) Do the smoothing of the abradable material (Figure 812).
1) Put the roller set in position in front of the area to be smoothed.
NOTE: Smoothing is done in counterclockwise direction.
NOTE: Never superimpose two layers of polyester film.
2) Disengage the lift lever from its position to lower the scraping tool and roller set
(Figure 809).
3) Attach the polyester film to the containment case with a strip of 3M 471 tape,
G51486 [CP2109], to make sure that the polyester film stays tensioned.
4) Move the roller set to a speed between 0.06-0.12 in./sec. (1.5-3 mm/s).
NOTE: The speed must be slow to get a correct quality of flatness.
5) Make sure that there are no waves, no air bubbles and the edges are correctly cut.
If not, do again the adjustment of the angle and height of the smoothing rolls. Do the
step 2.F.(9)(a)10)b).
NOTE: If you are at the end of the last sector, go to step 2.F.(9)(e)9).
6) Cut the polyester film with the locally manufactured set square after each sector
when roll No. 3 is after the reconditioning area (Figure 813).
7) Put the scraping tool and roller set in upper position with the lift lever (Figure 809).
8) Do again steps 2.F.(9)(b) thru 2.F.(9)(e)7) for the other sectors or steps 2.F.(9)(b)
thru 2.F.(9)(e)5) for the last sector.
9) At the end of the last sector, remove roll No. 1 and roll No. 2 to complete smoothing
with roll No. 3 without smoothing the first sector again.
10) Cut the polyester film with the locally manufactured set square.
11) Put the scraping tool and roller set in upper position with the lift lever (Figure 809).
12) Wait for 12 hours minimum before you remove the polyester film and the colored
plastic tape.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(f) Removal of reconditioning fixture (Figure 814).
1) Make sure that the scraping blade and the roller set are in the upper position.
2) Remove the lift handle and put it in stored position (Figure 809).
3) Put the reconditioning dolly in position. Make sure that it is at the correct height.
4) Make sure that the two knurled buttons of the reconditioning dolly point in.
5) Engage the reconditioning dolly into the reconditioning fixture.
6) Attach the reconditioning dolly into the reconditioning fixture with the two knobs.
a) Unscrew the two knobs.
b) Turn the two knurled buttons out.
c) Tighten the two knobs to tightly attach the reconditioning dolly to the
reconditioning fixture.
7) Move up the slider with the handle to between 0.039 in. (1 mm) and 0.079 in.
(2 mm) to lift the reconditioning fixture.
8) Loosen the six knobs of the reconditioning fixture to release the reconditioning
fixture from the fan disk or from the dummy fan disk (Figure 814).
NOTE: Use the reverse sequence than for installation (3 to 1) (Figure 807).
9) Turn the six knurled buttons counterclockwise.
NOTE: The white mark on the knurled buttons must point in.
10) Remove the reconditioning fixture assembly with the reconditioning dolly.
(g) Reconditioning of the containment case.
1) Remove the carter protector of the reconditioning fixture, SPL-15838, by loosening
the wing nuts and put it on the reconditioning dolly (Figure 803).

F. High Pressure Compressor Front Stator Inspection
SUBTASK 72-32-00-900-001-F00
(1) If you find damage that is not in the limits, replace the engine, unless you are given other
instructions (TASK 71-00-02-000-801-F00 and TASK 71-00-02-400-801-F00).
SUBTASK 72-32-00-210-001-F00
(2) Look for damage to the Front Stator Case:
(a) Cracks
1) Cracks are not permitted.
2) A Continue-in-Service limit is 10 cycles or 25 hours, if the cracks in the skin are less
than 0.17 in. (4.3 mm) in length and there are no cracks in the flanges.
(b) Nicks, pits, marks, and scratches
1) All nicks, pits, marks, and scratches are permitted if the damage is not more than
0.050 in. (1.3 mm) in depth.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) The Continue-in-Service limit is 10 cycles or 25 hours for nicks, pits, marks, and
scratches that are more than the limit.
SUBTASK 72-32-00-210-002-F00
(3) Look for damage to the actuation rings:
(a) Cracks
1) Cracks are not permitted.
2) The Continue-in-Service limits are as follows:
a) Do an inspection again in or less than 200 cycles if a crack is found but does
not extend into adjacent transition radius.
b) Replace actuation ring in or less than 200 cycles if a crack is found that
connects 2 adjacent ring sides.
c) Replace actuation ring in or less than 5 cycles if a crack is found that connects
3 or more ring sides.
(b) Distortion, bends, or twists
1) Distortion, bends, or twists are not permitted.
2) A Continue-in-Service limit of 5 cycles is permitted, if there is no separation of the
actuation rings.
(c) Separation
1) Separation is not permitted.
(d) Missing bushings on Stages 1 and 2
1) Up to three missing bushings for each stage permitted.
2) If four missing bushings for each stage are found, repair within 200 cycles
(TASK 72-32-00-900-801-F00).
3) If five or more missing bushings for each stage are found, replace the actuation ring
flange bushing (TASK 72-32-00-900-801-F00).
(e) Missing bushings on Stage 3
1) Up to three missing bushings permitted.
2) If you find four missing bushings, replace the actuation ring bushings in or less than
200 cycles (TASK 72-32-00-900-802-F00).
3) If you find five or more missing bushings, replace the actuation ring bushings
(TASK 72-32-00-900-802-F00).
(f) Missing or broken bushing legs
1) Missing or broken bushing legs are permitted.
SUBTASK 72-32-00-210-003-F00
(4) Look for damage to the connecting links:
(a) Cracks in the connecting links on only one side of the engine
1) Cracks are not permitted.
2) A Continue-in-Service limit of 5 cycles is permitted, if the cracked connector link is
replaced.
(b) Cracks in the connecting links on the two sides of the engine
1) Cracks are not permitted.
(c) Missing bushings
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Missing bushings are not permitted. Replace the connecting link
(TASK 72-32-00-900-804-F00).
SUBTASK 72-32-00-220-001-F00
(5) Look for damage to the IGV and stage 3 lever arms:
(a) Broken IGV and stage 3 lever arms
1) Broken arms are not permitted.
2) A Continue-in-Service limit for the engine of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted, if
you replace the broken lever arm.
(b) Lever arms that are not engaged in the actuation ring or connecting link
1) This condition is not permitted.
(c) Cracked, bent, or twisted lever arms
1) Cracked, bent, or twisted lever arms are not permitted.
2) Do these steps:
a) Remove the lever arm.
b) Compare the removed lever arm with a new lever arm in an optical comparator
(P/N: 2202500) to find the angle of the bend or twist.
c) For a removed lever arm that has a bent or twisted angle of less than 4
degrees, install a new lever arm and put the engine back into service.
d) For a removed lever arm that has a bent or twisted angle of 4 degrees or
more, install a new lever arm before you put the engine back into service and
replace the engine before 10 cycles or 25 hours.
(d) Nicks, dents, and scratches
1) Replace the lever arm if the damage is more than the limits that follow.
2) Nicks, dents, and scratches in Area A are not permitted.
3) All nicks, dents, and scratches in Area B that are not more than 0.010 in. (0.25 mm)
in depth are permitted after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal
of High Metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00).
a) Sharp points at the bottom of the nicks, dents, and scratches are not
permitted.
4) All nicks, pits, marks, and scratches in area C that are not more than 0.002 in.
(0.05 mm) in depth are permitted after you remove the high metal. Refer to General
Removal of High Metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00).
NOTE: The limits do not apply to the pin.
(e) Do a check for loose variable stator vanes.
1) There is no maximum limit of radial and side motion if the bushing is in place and if
there is no metal-to-metal contact.
NOTE: Shake the vane stem. Listen for metal-to-metal contact.
a) Replace the bushing if it is missing (TASK 72-32-00-900-802-F00).
SUBTASK 72-32-00-220-002-F00
(6) Look for damage to the stage 1 and 2 lever arms:
(a) Cracked, broken, bent, or twisted lever arms
1) This condition is not permitted.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Lever arms that are not engaged into the actuation ring or connector link
1) This condition is not permitted.
(c) Nicks, dents, and scratches in the lever arms
1) Replace the engine if these limits are more than permitted.
2) Nicks, dents, and scratches in Area A are not permitted.
3) All nicks, dents, and scratches in Area B that are not more than 0.010 in. (0.25 mm)
in depth are permitted after you remove the high metal. Refer to General Removal
of High Metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00).
a) Sharp points at the bottom of the nicks, dents, and scratches are not
permitted.
4) All nicks, pits, marks, and scratches in area C that are not more than 0.002 in.
(0.05 mm) in depth are permitted after you remove the high metal. Refer to General
Removal of High Metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00).
NOTE: The limits do not apply to the pin.
(d) Do a check for loose variable stator vanes.
1) There is no maximum limit of radial and side motion if the bushing is in place and if
there is no metal-to-metal contact.
NOTE: Shake the vane stem. Listen for metal-to-metal contact.
2) If you hear metal-to-metal contact, replace the engine (TASK 71-00-02-000-801-F00
and TASK 71-00-02-400-801-F00).
3) A maximum service extension of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted if there is
metal-to-metal contact on no more than 50% of the vanes.
SUBTASK 72-32-00-220-003-F00
(7) Examine the bellcrank assemblies (two locations):

(1) Disconnect the tie-rods [28] from the actuation ring clevises (TASK 72-32-00-900-805-F00).
(a) On each VSV stage, remove the D-head bolts [70] and self-locking nuts [80] that attach

SUBTASK 72-32-00-200-001-F00
(2) Perform a VSV resistance (force) check for IGV, Stage 1, Stage 2, and Stage 3 as follows:
(a) For each VSV stage, attach a push-pull digital force gauge, COM-1822, or equivalent
force indicator to the clevis of each actuation ring and pull the actuation ring to rotate the
stage from open to closed, and then back to open.

(c) Make sure that each VSV stage requires not more than 100 lbf (445 N) to move the
actuation ring.

G. High Pressure Compressor Stage 4 Vane Trailing Edge Inspection
SUBTASK 72-32-00-210-010-F00
(1) Do an inspection of the HPC stage 4 vane trailing edge:
(a) Do a borescope inspection (BSI) of the HPC airfoils and look for erosion of the airfoil
corners and chord (TASK 72-00-00-200-804-F00).
(b) Do a special flexible BSI of the HPC stage 4 vane sector trailing edges for erosion as
follows (Figure 605):
1) Use the borescope resolution monitor, COM-9899, to make sure that the fiber
borescope, COM-2196, is serviceable.
2) Connect the fiber light cable to the fiber borescope, COM-2196.
3) Put the flexible light source, SPL-2197, into the LPT bleed port on the HPC front
stator at the 10:30 o'clock position.
4) Put the flexible light source, SPL-2197, through the HPC stage 4 vane sector bleed
slot.
NOTE: You can see five or six vane sector bleed slots through the LPT bleed port.
It is recommended to do an inspection in at least two or three positions to
get the best viewing angle of the vane sector trailing edge.
5) Articulate the scope to get a focus on the vane sector trailing edge.
6) Look for erosion on the HPC stage 4 vane sector trailing edge, especially near the
outer platform (Figure 605, Figure 606, and Figure 607).
7) Re-inspection intervals depend on the amount of serviceable distress found.
a) If no erosion is found, then re-inspect before 4,800 cycles.
b) If the trailing edge is eroded but not axially past the start of the bleed slot, then
re-inspect before 1,600 cycles (Figure 605).
c) If the trailing edge is eroded axially past the start of the bleed slot, then
remove engine before 100 cycles.
8) Slowly pull the flexible light source, SPL-2197, back out of the port after you
complete the inspection.

F. Lever Arms and Bushings (IGV and Stage 3) Replacement
SUBTASK 72-32-00-020-003-F00
(1) Remove the lever arm and bushings.
(a) Hold the lever arm with the anti-torque lever, SPL-9071, to make sure the vane does not
turn.
(b) Remove the nut and washer from the vane stem.
(c) Use the lever arm puller, SPL-9072, to remove the lever arm from the vane.
(d) If it is necessary, remove the bushings from the stator case and actuation ring.
(e) If you install the shims, remove and discard the shims from the 3rd-stage vanes.
SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-002-F00
(2) Install the lever arm and bushings.
(a) If it is necessary, install new bushings in the stator case and actuation ring.
(b) Install the lever arm as follows:
CAUTION
YOU MUST ALIGN THE ROUNDED END OF THE LEVER ARM SLOT
WITH THE ROUNDED END OF THE VANE TRUNNION. IF YOU DO
NOT ALIGN THE VANE CORRECTLY, ENGINE DAMAGE WILL
OCCUR.
1) Align the rounded end of the lever arm slot with the rounded end of the vane stem.
a) If the vane stem has a witness mark, the lever arm is installed correctly when
the mark is on the same side as the rounded end of the lever arm slot.
2) Put the lever arm on the vane stem.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
3) Engage the lever arm pin in the actuation ring.
4) Make sure the lever arm fully engages with the vane stem tang.
(c) While you hold the lever arm with the anti-torque lever, SPL-9071, to make sure the vane
does not turn, install the nut and washer from the vane stem.
1) Tighten the nut to 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m) - 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m).

WARNING

CAUTION

DO MOVE THE ADJUSTABLE LINK, YOU MUST ADJUST THE ADJUSTABLE
LINK AGAIN. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THIS PRECAUTION, INCORRECT

(1) Disconnect the tie rod [7] from the clevis of the defective connecting link [1] as follows:

(3) Remove the bolts [2] that hold the connecting link [1] to the actuation ring [5].
NOTE: There is a locating pin at each end of the connecting link. The straight pin stays in the
actuation ring segment. The pin with the head comes out with the connecting link.

SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-015-F00
(3) Install the connecting link [1] to the actuation ring [5] segments.
(a) Make sure the trapped straight pin [4] fully engages the hole in the actuation ring [5].
NOTE: Make sure the lever arms are correctly installed in the connecting link bushings.
SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-016-F00
(4) Install the headed pin [3] in the connecting link [1] and actuation ring [5] segment.
SUBTASK 72-32-00-640-003-F00
(5) Apply graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101] to the threads and friction surface of the
bolt [2].
SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-017-F00
(6) Install the bolt [2].

ARMS CORRECTLY.

G. Procedure
SUBTASK 72-32-00-000-002-F00
(1) Remove the left or right VSV actuator (TASK 75-31-01-000-801-F00 or
TASK 75-31-01-000-802-F00).
SUBTASK 72-32-00-020-010-F00
(2) Do these steps to remove the VSV Bellcrank Assembly:
(a) Remove the D-head bolts [70] and self-locking nuts [80] that attach the rod-ends of the
connecting links to the actuation ring clevises.
(b) Remove the bolt [20], bolt [21], washers [30], bolt [23], bolt [25], and washers [40] that
attach the VSV bellcrank to the stator case.
(c) Remove the VSV bellcrank assembly from the engine.
NOTE: A check of the HPC VSV system resistance, as specified in
TASK 72-32-00-200-803-F00 of the VSV Bellcrank Assembly, is required prior to
return to service.
SUBTASK 72-32-00-300-001-F00
(3) Do the repair of the VSV actuator system hardware:
(a) Do this task: Variable Stator Vane (VSV) Actuator System Hardware Repair,
TASK 72-32-00-900-806-F00.
SUBTASK 72-32-00-200-002-F00
(4) Do a resistance (force) check of the Variable Stator Vane (VSV) System for IGV, Stage 1,
Stage 2, and Stage 3 (TASK 72-32-00-200-803-F00).
(a) Remove the engine if any stage requires more than 100 lbf (445 N) to move the actuation
ring.
SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-023-F00
(5) Do these steps to install VSV Bellcrank Assembly:
(a) Clean the component interface and/or the adjacent area.
(b) Do a visual inspection of the component interface and/or the adjacent area.
(c) Install the VSV bellcrank assembly as follows:
1) Apply graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101] to the bolt [20], bolt [21],
bolt [23], and bolt [25].
2) Install the mounting sleeve [50] on the head-end side of the assembly.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) Put the sleeve [50] on the inboard side of the bellcrank mounting boss on the
connecting link side.
b) Position the actuation assembly on the mounting boss and align the bolt holes.
3) Attach both mounting bosses, on the head-end side of the assembly, with two
washers [30] and the bolt [20] and bolt [21].
4) Install the mounting sleeve [50] on the rod-end side of the actuator.
a) Put the sleeve [50] on the inboard side of the bellcrank mounting boss on the
connecting link side.
b) Position the actuation assembly on the mounting boss and align the bolt holes.
5) Attach the mounting boss, on the rod-end and connecting link side of the assembly,
with the washer [40] and bolt [23].
6) Attach the mounting boss, on the rod-end and actuator side of the assembly, with
mounting spacer [60], washer [40], and bolt [25].
7) Tighten the two head-end bolt [20] and bolt [21] to between 110 in-lb (12.43 N·m)
and 120 in-lb (13.56 N·m).
a) Install the safety wire, G02345 [CP8001] or safety wire, G02495 [CP8002] on
the mounting bolts (TASK 70-20-01-800-804-F00).
8) Tighten the two rod-end bolt [23] and bolt [25] to between 215 in-lb (24.29 N·m) and
225 in-lb (25.42 N·m).
a) Install the safety wire, G02345 [CP8001] or safety wire, G02495 [CP8002] on
the mounting bolts (TASK 70-20-01-800-804-F00).
9) Lubricate the threads of the D-head bolts [70] and self-locking nuts [80] with
graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101].
10) Install the rod-ends of the connecting links to the actuation ring clevises and secure
with D-head bolts [70] and self-locking nuts [80].
NOTE: The bolt head goes aft for IGV and forward for stages 1, 2, and 3.
11) Tighten the self-locking nuts [80] to between 62 in-lb (7.01 N·m) and 68 in-lb
(7.68 N·m).
SUBTASK 72-32-00-420-024-F00
(6) Install the left or right VSV actuator (TASK 75-31-01-400-801-F00 or
TASK 75-31-01-400-802-F00).

(a) Remove the nuts [11], washers [12], bolts [13], nut [14], washer [15], bolt [16], and
bushing [17] that attach the master rod [19] to the bellcrank assemblies.
(b) Remove the master rod [19].
(c) Remove the nuts [1] and bolts [2] that attach the bellcranks to the support plates.
(d) Remove the upper support plate [4].
(e) Remove the bellcrank [7], bellcrank [8], bellcrank [9], and bellcrank [10].

(g) Remove the sleeves [6] from the bellcranks.

(i) Remove the tie rod [24], tie rod [25], tie rod [26], and tie rod [27].

(3) Do these steps to assemble the left or right VSV actuator support assembly (Figure 806 or
Figure 807):

rod [25], and tie rod [26]) with bolts [23] and nuts [22].
NOTE: The nuts must be installed with no lubricant and must have a minimum run-on
torque of 5 in-lb (0.56 N·m).
1) The stage identification on the bellcrank goes up (Figure 808).
2) The bolt goes up through the short end of the bellcrank (Figure 808).
(b) Tighten the nuts [22] to 55 in-lb (6 N·m) - 70 in-lb (8 N·m).
(c) Install the bolts [2] up through the lower support plate [3] in the stage 1 and 2 positions.
(d) Install the sleeves [6] in the lower support plate [3] at the IGV, stage 1, 2, and 3 positions.
(e) Install the bushings [5] on the sleeves [6].
1) The flange goes down.
(f) Install the bellcrank [7] on the bushings at the IGV position.
1) The stage identification on the bellcrank goes up.
(g) Install the stage 1-3 bellcranks (bellcrank [8], bellcrank [9], and bellcrank [10]).
(h) Install the upper support plate [4].
(i) Install the bolt [2] in the support assembly at the IGV position.
1) The head of the bolt goes up.
(j) Install the nuts [1].
NOTE: The nuts must be installed with no lubricant and must have a minimum run-on
torque of 5 in-lb (0.56 N·m).
(k) Tighten the nuts [1] to 55 in-lb (6 N·m) - 70 in-lb (8 N·m).
(l) Apply graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101], to the bearing surfaces of the master
rod [19].
(m) Attach the master rod [19] to the IGV, stage 1 and stage 2 bellcranks with bolts [13],
washers [12], and nuts [11].
1) The bolt head goes up at the IGV position and down at the stage 1 and 2 positions.
(n) Install the bushing [17] at the stage 3 position.
1) The flange goes down.
(o) Install the bolt [16] at the stage 3 position.
1) The head of the bolt goes up.

(p) Install the washer [15] and nut [14].

(q) Tighten the nut [14] to 55 in-lb (6 N·m) - 70 in-lb (8 N·m).
(r) Attach the stage 3 bellcrank [10] to the stage 3 tie rod [27] with bolt [23] and nut [22].
NOTE: The nut must be installed with no lubricant and must have a minimum run-on

(4) Do these steps to examine the free play of the tie rod [24], tie rod [25], tie rod [26], and tie

(b) Use C-clamps to hold the assembly to the angle plate.

SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-001-F00
(1) Look for damage on the aft flange (Figure 601):
(a) Cracks that connect the bolt holes
1) Not serviceable.
a) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles is permitted for one crack, if the crack
connects two bolt holes and does not go into the outer skin of the pressure
vessel.
(b) Cracks that extend from the bolt holes to the outer edge of the flange
1) It is permitted to have 5 cracks with a minimum of 5 holes of separation between the
cracks.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(c) Cracks that extend from the bolt holes to the casing skin
1) Not serviceable.
a) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles is permitted for one crack that extends
0.4 inch (10.2 mm) into the skin.
(d) Cracks in other areas of the flange
1) It is permitted to have 5 cracks on each flange if they are not more than 0.25 inch
(6.35 mm) in length with this condition:
a) A minimum of 5.0 inches (127.0 mm) of separation between all other cracks.
(e) Cracks in the skin radius of the flange and case
1) Not serviceable.
(f) Nicks, scores and scratches
1) There is no limit to the number of nicks, scores, scratches with these limits:
a) Not more than 1.0 inch (25.4 mm) long.
b) Not more than 0.01 inch (0.25 mm) in depth after you remove the high metal.
Refer to General Removal of High Metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance
Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00).
c) There is a minimum separation of 1.0 inch (25.4 mm) with other damage.
SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-002-F00
(2) Look for damage on the casing skin:
(a) Cracks in the parent metal
1) All cracks that are not more than 0.04 inch (1.0 mm) in length and have a minimum
separation of 2.0 inches (50.8 mm).
a) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles is permitted for one crack which is not
more than 0.4 inch (10.16 mm) in length.
(b) Nicks and scratches
1) All nicks and scratches 0.01 inch (0.25 mm) in depth are permitted after you remove
the high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal (Hand Blending -
Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00).
(c) Dents
1) All dents with a maximum depth of 0.02 inch (0.5 mm) are permitted if they have a
smooth contour.
SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-003-F00
(3) Look for damage on all ports that have threads:

1) No more than one complete thread can be removed or the total damage for all
threads cannot be more than one thread, after you chase the threads.

(a) Cracks
1) Not serviceable.
(b) Finding on threads
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)

 ALL
1) Any amount not more than 1/2 full thread after removal of high metal. Refer to

a) A Continue-In Service limit of 10 cycles is permitted.

(5) Look for damage on the ring sector support:

1) Not serviceable.

(b) Cracks

SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-009-F00
(7) Look for damage on the T49.5 probe thermocouple studs:
(a) Broken or missing stud
1) Not serviceable.
a) Do the repair of the broken stud (TASK 72-54-00-300-801-F00).
b) A continue in service limit of 20 cycles is permitted until the broken stud is
repaired with these conditions:
<1> Damage is limited to one stud per T49.5 sensor.
NOTE: Each T49.5 sensor has two probes, each probe is attached to

<2> A visual inspection of the area of the broken stud shows no indication of
air leak.
<3> A visual check makes sure there is no obvious gap between the probe

SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-006-F00
(8) Look for damage on the cooling air manifold (Figure 602):
(a) Cracks in the forward mounting lug
1) One crack on each side of a lug is permitted.
(b) A broken forward mounting lug
1) Breakage on one side of a mounting lug is permitted.
2) Breakage or a crack on each side of a forward lug is permitted if the two adjacent
cooling air tube supports are not broken or have a crack that is not more than 0.591
inch (15.0 mm) in length.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
3) If there is breakage or a crack on each side of a forward lug, and the two adjacent
cooling air tube supports are broken or have a crack that is more than 0.591 inch
(15.0 mm), these are the Continue-In-Service limits:
a) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 hours or 10 cycles is permitted if one
adjacent support is broken.
b) If one or two adjacent supports have a crack that is more than 0.591 inch (15.0
mm) long, examine the part at not more than 10 hours or 10 cycles to see if
the crack length increases.
c) If you find that the crack length did not increase, then repeat the check at not
more than 50 hours or 50 cycles, and then at each 100 hours or 100 cycles
until the part is repaired or the crack length increases.
d) If you find that the crack length increases, a Continue-In-Service limit of 30
hours or 30 cycles is permitted.
(c) Cracks in the sheet metal
1) All cracks are permitted with these limits:
a) The cracks are not longer than 0.5 inch (12.7 mm).
b) The total length of all cracks is not longer than 3.0 inches (76.2 mm).
c) The cracks have a minimum separation of 1.0 inch (25.4 mm) between each
crack.
(d) Dents on sleeve
1) All dents are permitted if they have a smooth contour and are not more than 0.03
inch (0.76 mm) in depth.
(e) Nick, scratch and chafing (wear) on tube external surface
1) Maximum finish depth after you make the defect smooth is 0.008 inch (0.20 mm).
a) Make the defect smooth by hand blending (CFMI CFM56 Standard Practices
Manual 70-41-11) if necessary to remove sharp edges.
b) Make sure there is no crack. Do this task: Fluorescent Penetrant Inspection
(Portable Post-Emulsifiable), TASK 70-40-01-230-801-F00.
(f) Scratches and chafing on box
1) All scratches and chafing are permitted if they are not more than 0.004 in. (0.1 mm)
in depth.
(g) Dents on box
1) All dents are permitted if they are without sharp edge and are not more than
0.118 in. (3.0 mm) in depth.
SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-007-F00
(9) Look for damage on the cooling air tubes:
(a) Cracks in tubes
1) All cracks are permitted if not longer than 2.0 inch (50.8 mm) and separated by at
least one support member.
(b) Dents
1) All dents are permitted if they have a smooth contour and are not more than 20
percent of the tube outside diameter.
(c) Cracks in tube clamps

 ALL
1) All cracks are permitted if the tubes are correctly attached.

1) All cracks are permitted if the supports are not loose.
(b) Cracks in all other areas
1) All cracks are permitted if the cooling air tubes and fasteners are not loose.
(c) Breakage of the forward mount lug
1) One broken lug is permitted for one-half of the distribution manifold.
SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-011-F00
(11) Look for damage on the LPTACC cooling air manifold:

(b) Dents and collapse

1) All flat areas are permitted if contour change is not more than 5 percent of the tube.
SUBTASK 72-54-00-210-012-F00
(12) Look for damage on the LPTACC cooling air duct:

1) No cracks are permitted.
(b) Dents and collapse
1) All dents and collapse are permitted if depth is not more than 5 percent of the outer

(c) Flat area
1) All flat areas are permitted if contour change is not more than 5 percent of the tube.

2. Replacement of Broken Studs on the T49.5 Probe Bracket Assembly
(Figure 801, Figure 802, Figure 803, Figure 804)
A. General
(1) This procedure contains one task: to replace the broken studs on the T49.5 Probe Bracket
Assembly.
(2) If you find a broken stud on the bracket assembly, replace the broken stud if there is sufficient
access.
NOTE: The replacement of the broken studs depend on accessibility.
NOTE: Make sure that free access is available for the drilling and tapping procedure.
NOTE: You must discard the repaired bracket assembly at the first LPT rotor/stator
disassembly.
(3) The T49.5 probe (and thermocouple) bracket assemblies are installed on the LPT case at 2:00,
5:00, 7:30 and 10: 00 o’clock position and below the air cooling tubes.

E. Procedure
SUBTASK 72-54-00-010-003-F00
WARNING
DO ALL OF THE SPECIFIED TASKS IN THE CORRECT SEQUENCE TO OPEN
THE THRUST REVERSER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THIS INSTRUCTION,
INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(1) Do this task: Open the Thrust Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-801-F00.
SUBTASK 72-54-00-010-004-F00
WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENTS OF THE OIL SYSTEM IF THE ENGINE
IS HOT. THESE COMPONENTS STAY HOTTER THAN OTHER
COMPONENTS. HOT COMPONENTS CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT OPEN THE OIL SYSTEM UNTIL THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO.
THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES AFTER AN
ENGINE STOPS. A PRESSURIZED OIL SYSTEM CAN RELEASE A SPRAY OF
HOT OIL THAT CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON YOU. PUT ON CLOTHES, GOGGLES, AND
OTHER EQUIPMENT FOR PROTECTION, OR LET THE ENGINE BECOME
COOL. HOT OIL CAN BURN YOU.
CAUTION
DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON THE ENGINE OR OTHER COMPONENTS.
IMMEDIATELY CLEAN THE COMPONENT IF OIL FALLS ON IT. OIL CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO PAINT AND RUBBER.
NOTE: The engine oil is poisonous. Use the personal protection equipment. Put the lubrication unit
on the clean bench in a good ventilated area.
(2) Do this task: T49.5 Probe Removal, TASK 77-21-01-000-801-F00.
SUBTASK 72-54-00-010-005-F00
WARNING
DO NOT BREATHE THE PARTICLES, OR GET THEM IN YOUR MOUTH,
EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. PUT ON A RESPIRATOR, GOGGLES, AND
GLOVES AND OTHER EQUIPMENT FOR PROTECTION. THESE PARTICLES
CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
WARNING
USE EYE PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COMPRESSED AIR TO CLEAN,
COOL, OR DRY PARTS OR TOOLS. PARTICLES CAN CAUSE AN INJURY TO
YOUR EYES. DO NOT USE MORE THAN 30 PSI (207 KPA). DO NOT POINT
COMPRESSED AIR AT YOURSELF OR OTHER PERSONS.
(3) Use a square access to remove the nuts and the bulkheads.
NOTE: It is easier to use a square access to remove the nuts, with bulkheads removed.
SUBTASK 72-54-00-320-001-F00
(4) Do these steps to prepare for the broken stud drilling.
(a) Calculate the length of the remaining broken tack welded stud shank with the serviceable
remaining tack welded stud.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Do these steps to install a locally manufactured tool on the serviceable remaining tack
welded stud.
1) Make sure that you correctly engaged the center pin of the tooling in the bore of the
T49.5 probe location.
2) Tighten the tooling to the LPT case with the original nut on the serviceable
remaining tack welded stud.
3) Make sure that the tooling is correctly installed against the LPT case.
(c) Make a selection to get the correct drill guide sleeve for a 0.25 inch (6.35 mm) drill.
NOTE: You can identify the sleeve as the clearance guide.
(d) Install the retaining screw between the drill guide sleeve and the tooling.
(e) Do a check from the top of the drill guide sleeve to the T49.5 probe location of the LPT
case.
SUBTASK 72-54-00-910-001-F00
NOTE: Do not drill into the stud head when you remove the broken stud shank. Refer to the
Standard Practices Manual (Refer to CFMI SPM, Task 70-44-50-320-006) before you drill
the hole into the stud head.
NOTE: When you do the drilling and tapping operation, use a minimum pressure to do these
operations. If you put too much pressure, you can push the fitting away from the inside of
the LPT case, as it is only safe tied by a good tack welded stud on one side.
(5) Do these steps to drill the broken stud shank.
(a) Calculate the necessary drill depth with the dimensions given in the above step and the
dimensions shown in the figure to remove the broken stud shank.
(b) Make a selection to get the correct drilling stop ring for the 0.25 inch (6.35 mm) drill.
(c) Attach the stop ring to the 0.25 inch (6.35 mm) diameter drill.
1) Set it to the depth as calculated as in the above steps.
(d) Put the drill into the tooling sleeve.
(e) Drill to a depth permitted by the stop ring to remove the remaining broken stud shank.
SUBTASK 72-54-00-910-002-F00
(6) Do these steps to prepare for tack welded stud head drilling.
(a) Remove the drill guide sleeve (identified as “clearance guide”).
(b) Replace it with the other drill guide sleeve (identified as “tapping drill guide”) for a 0.211
inch (5.36 mm) drill.
(c) Do a check from the top of the drilling sleeve to the T49.5 probe location of the LPT case.
(d) Calculate the drill depth (use the dimensions given before and the dimensions shown in
the Figure) to drill through the tack welded stud head and the back plate.
NOTE: You must be careful when you drill, and make sure that it does not break through
the back plate.
SUBTASK 72-54-00-910-003-F00
NOTE: If you do an incorrect calculation of the drill depth and setting of the drill depth stop ring, you
may have a risk to go through the insulation blanket. In this case, you must do the full
disassembly of the LPT rotor/stator.
(7) Do these steps to drill the tack welded stud head.

 ALL
(a) Install a correct stop ring to drill a 0.211 inch (5.36 mm) diameter hole.
NOTE: The stop ring is identified with a drill size of 0.211 inch (5.36 mm).
NOTE: Set it to the depth specified as calculated in the “Drilling of the broken stud
shank” as in the paragraph above.
(b) Put the drill into the tooling sleeve.
NOTE: When you perform the drilling operation, and if you find that you have too much
depth, you go to drill through the insulation blanket.
(c) Drill to a depth permitted by the stop ring to drill the stud head and the back plate.
(d) Remove the drill guide sleeve (identified as “tapping drill guide”).
(e) Replace it with the other drill guide sleeve (identified as “clearance guide”).
SUBTASK 72-54-00-910-004-F00
(8) Do these steps to tap the tack welded stud head.
(a) Do a check from the top of the drill guide sleeve to the T49.5 probe location of the LPT
case.
(b) Calculate the specified tap depth with the dimensions given before and the dimensions
shown in the figure, to tap through the tack welded stud head and the back plate only.
(c) Set the 0.25 inch (6.35 mm) stop ring to the specified depth with the tap given in the
tooling.
(d) Put the tap into the tooling sleeve.
(e) Tap the head of the tack welded stud and the back plate.
NOTE: Refer to CFMI SPM, Task 70-44-60-320-007.
(f) Make sure that you vacuum all the unwanted particles.
(g) Remove the nut.
(h) Remove the tooling.
SUBTASK 72-54-00-470-001-F00
(9) Do these steps to install the T49.5 probe on the reworked bracket.
(a) To identify the repair, write the bulletin number CFM 56-7B-72-0423 on the locally
manufactured washer (Refer to CFMI SPM, Task 70-10-12-350-005).
(b) Do this task: T49.5 Probe Installation, TASK 77-21-01-400-801-F00.
(c) Install the locally manufactured washer with the lockwire hole below the nut at the
location adjacent to the modified broken tack welded stud.
(d) Apply a light layer of the lubricant, D50068 [CP2544] on the remaining stud thread and on
the new bolt thread.
(e) Install the bolt (GE part number J644P09B) on the modified tapped tack welded stud
head.
NOTE: Make sure that you have the washer correctly located to the lockwire adjacent
bolt.
(f) Tighten the nut and bolt to 100.0-110.0 Pound-inches (11.5-12.5 Newton-meters).

(g) Lock the bolt to the washer below the nut with a safety wire, G02345 [CP8001] or the
safety cable, G50065 [CP8006] (Lockwire Installation, TASK 70-20-01-800-804-F00).
NOTE: If you have the second stud broken, in addition to the already replaced stud, you
can do this repair to replace this second broken stud by a bolt. You must safety
the bolts together with a lockwire in the head bolt holes. Keep the locally

(h) Do a check from the top of the T49.5 probe to the LPT case.
NOTE: You must not have lack of protrusion between the bolt end and the tapped stud
head.
(i) Make sure that the value of the protrusion is correct.
NOTE: You must calculate the protrusion of the bolt thread through the modified tack
welded stud head with the dimension used to find the bolt length in the figures.

H. LPT Shaft-Plug O-ring Replacement
SUBTASK 72-55-00-020-001-F00
WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENTS OF THE OIL SYSTEM IF THE ENGINE
IS HOT. THESE COMPONENTS STAY HOTTER THAN OTHER
COMPONENTS. HOT COMPONENTS CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT OPEN THE OIL SYSTEM UNTIL THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO.
THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES AFTER AN
ENGINE STOPS. A PRESSURIZED OIL SYSTEM CAN RELEASE A SPRAY OF
HOT OIL THAT CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON YOU. PUT ON CLOTHES, GOGGLES, AND
OTHER EQUIPMENT FOR PROTECTION, OR LET THE ENGINE BECOME
COOL. HOT OIL CAN BURN YOU.
CAUTION
DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON THE ENGINE OR OTHER COMPONENTS.
IMMEDIATELY CLEAN THE COMPONENT IF OIL FALLS ON IT. OIL CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO PAINT AND RUBBER.
(1) Do these steps to replace the LPT Shaft-Plug O-ring [3] and O-rings [4].
(a) Remove the retaining ring [5] from forward end of the LPT shaft [1], with a scribe.
(b) Remove the LPT shaft plug [2] with the puller adapter, SPL-6180, or puller, SPL-11207.
(c) Remove and discard O-ring [3] and two O-rings [4] located in the forward/aft grooves of
the LPT shaft plug [2].
(d) Remove the puller adapter, SPL-6180, or puller, SPL-11207, from the LPT shaft plug [2].
WARNING
ACETONE IS AN AGENT THAT IS FLAMMABLE, EXPLOSIVE,
POISONOUS, AND AN IRRITANT. MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS OBEY ALL
OF THE PRECAUTIONS WHEN ACETONE IS USED.
• GAS/AIR MIXTURES MORE THAN THE LOWER EXPLOSIVE LIMIT
(LEL) CAN CAUSE AN EXPLOSION IF HIGH HEAT, SPARKS, OR
FLAMES SUPPLY IGNITION.
• USE IN AN AREA OPEN TO THE AIR.
• CLOSE THE CONTAINER WHEN NOT USED.
• DO NOT GET ACETONE IN THE EYES, ON THE SKIN, OR ON YOUR
CLOTHES.
• DO NOT BREATHE THE GAS.
(e) Clean the oil stains on the plug grooves with acetone solvent, E50001.
(f) Install the LPT shaft plug [2] in the storage box.
WARNING
DO NOT LET THE ENGINE OIL STAY ON YOUR SKIN. ENGINE OIL IS
POISONOUS. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES. USE ENGINE OIL IN AN
AREA WITH GOOD AIRFLOW. DO NOT GET ENGINE OIL ON YOUR
CLOTHES OR ON THE AIRPLANE. ENGINE OIL CAN CAUSE INJURIES.
(g) Lightly coat new O-ring [3] and two new O-rings [4] with oil, D00599 [CP2442].
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU CORRECTLY INSTALL NEW O-RING IN THE
SEAL GROOVES AT THE FORWARD END AND THE AFT END OF THE
LPT SHAFT-PLUG. IF THE O-RING IS NOT CORRECTLY INSTALLED,
DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE CAN OCCUR.
(h) Install the new O-ring [3] and two new O-rings [4] into the seal grooves of the LPT shaft
plug [2].
(i) Install the LPT shaft plug [2] assembly into the forward end of the LPT shaft [1] and onto
the CVT.
NOTE: Insert the lug of the LPT shaft-plug in aligned slots of the LPT coupling nut and
the LPT shaft.
(j) Install the retaining ring [5] onto the LPT shaft [1].
(k) Do a visual inspection to make sure the correct installation of the retaining ring [5].

H. CVT O-rings and Damper Seals Replacement
SUBTASK 72-55-00-020-002-F00
WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENTS OF THE OIL SYSTEM IF THE ENGINE
IS HOT. THESE COMPONENTS STAY HOTTER THAN OTHER
COMPONENTS. HOT COMPONENTS CAN BURN YOU.

EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(WARNING PRECEDES)
WARNING
DO NOT OPEN THE OIL SYSTEM UNTIL THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO.
THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES AFTER AN
ENGINE STOPS. A PRESSURIZED OIL SYSTEM CAN RELEASE A SPRAY OF
HOT OIL THAT CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON YOU. PUT ON CLOTHES, GOGGLES, AND
OTHER EQUIPMENT FOR PROTECTION, OR LET THE ENGINE BECOME

CAUTION
DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON THE ENGINE OR OTHER COMPONENTS.
