CAUSE DAMAGE TO PAINT AND RUBBER.
CAUTION
REPLACE THE O-RING AND DAMPER SEALS IN ENGINE WARM CONDITION
IN LESS THAN TWO HOURS AFTER ENGINE SHUT DOWN. THE O-RING
AND DAMPER SEALS REMOVAL ARE EASY WHEN THE ENGINE IS IN
WARM CONDITION. IF YOU DO NOT, DAMAGE CAN OCCUR.
(1) Do these steps to replace the CVT O-ring [13], O-ring [14], and three damper seals [15].
(a) Install the protective ring, SPL-6183, in position in the fan disk hole.
(b) Remove the retaining ring [12] from the forward end of the LPT shaft [10] with a scribe.
(c) Do these steps to install the pusher/puller, SPL-6182:
1) Screw the tube of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, into the center vent tube [11].
2) Install the support of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, on the fan disk flange with four
knurled screws.
3) Engage the plate of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, in the slot of the screw and attach
it with the knurled nut.
(d) Do these steps to remove the center vent tube [11]:
1) Manually turn clockwise the screw of fixture of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, to
disengage the center vent tube [11] from the LPT shaft [10].
NOTE: You can use a wrench if the counter torque is important.
2) Remove the support of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, from the fan disk flange.
3) Remove the center vent tube [11] equipped with the tube of the pusher/puller,
SPL-6182, from the LPT shaft [10].
4) Remove the tube of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, from the center vent tube [11].
(e) Remove and discard the O-ring [13] and O-ring [14] located in the forward/aft grooves of
the center vent tube [11].
(f) Remove and discard the damper seals [15] located in the other grooves of the center
vent tube [11].
(g) Remove the protective ring, SPL-6183, in position in the fan disk hole.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
WARNING
ACETONE IS AN AGENT THAT IS FLAMMABLE, EXPLOSIVE,
POISONOUS, AND AN IRRITANT. MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS OBEY ALL
OF THE PRECAUTIONS WHEN ACETONE IS USED.
• GAS/AIR MIXTURES MORE THAN THE LOWER EXPLOSIVE LIMIT

• CLOSE THE CONTAINER WHEN NOT USED.
• DO NOT GET ACETONE IN THE EYES, ON THE SKIN, OR ON YOUR
CLOTHES.
• DO NOT BREATHE THE GAS.
(h) Clean the oil stains with acetone solvent, E50001, on the center vent tube [11], in the
O-ring and damper seal grooves and in the inner diameter of the fan disk with a lint free
cloth.
(i) Install the center vent tube [11] in the storage box.
WARNING
DO NOT LET THE ENGINE OIL STAY ON YOUR SKIN. ENGINE OIL IS
POISONOUS. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES. USE ENGINE OIL IN AN
AREA WITH GOOD AIRFLOW. DO NOT GET ENGINE OIL ON YOUR
CLOTHES OR ON THE AIRPLANE. ENGINE OIL CAN CAUSE INJURIES.
(j) Lightly coat three new damper seals [15] with oil, D00599 [CP2442].
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU CORRECTLY INSTALL NEW DAMPER SEALS IN
THE SEAL GROOVES OF THE CENTER VENT TUBE. YOU MUST HAVE
THE PLATE FACE OF THE DAMPER SEALS POINTED TO OUTER OF
THE CENTER VENT TUBE. IF THE DAMPER SEALS ARE NOT
CORRECTLY INSTALLED, DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE CAN OCCUR.
(k) Install the three new damper seals [15] into the seal grooves of the center vent tube [11].
WARNING
DO NOT LET THE ENGINE OIL STAY ON YOUR SKIN. ENGINE OIL IS
POISONOUS. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES. USE ENGINE OIL IN AN
AREA WITH GOOD AIRFLOW. DO NOT GET ENGINE OIL ON YOUR
CLOTHES OR ON THE AIRPLANE. ENGINE OIL CAN CAUSE INJURIES.
(l) Lubricate the mating face of the rear vent tube with Molykote G Rapid Plus lubricant,
D00640 [CP2104], or Dow Corning 321 lubricant, D00641 [CP5062].
(m) Lightly coat new O-ring [13] and new O-ring [14] with oil, D00599 [CP2442].
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU CORRECTLY INSTALL THE NEW O-RING IN
THE SEAL GROOVE AT THE FORWARD END OF THE CENTER VENT
TUBE. IF THE O-RING IS NOT CORRECTLY INSTALLED, DAMAGE TO
THE ENGINE CAN OCCUR.
(n) Install the new O-ring [13] and new O-ring [14] into the seal groves of the center vent
tube [11].
(o) Install the protective ring, SPL-6183, in position in the fan disk hole.
(p) Do these steps to pre-install the center vent tube [11]:
1) Screw the tube of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, in the center vent tube [11].

EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU INSTALL THE CENTER VENT TUBE. IF
YOU CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE LPT SHAFT INTERNAL SUPPORTS

2) Align and install the center vent tube [11] into the LPT shaft [10].
3) Align the lug of the center vent tube [11] with the aligned slots of the LPT shaft [10]
and the LPT coupling.
(q) Do these steps to install the pusher/puller and center vent tube [11]:
1) Manually turn counter-clockwise the screw of fixture of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182,
to engage the center vent tube [11] into the slot of the LPT shaft [10].
NOTE: Be sure to stop turning the screw of the fixture of the pusher/puller before
the lug of the CVT touches the slot of the LPT Shaft.
NOTE: You can use a wrench if the counter torque is important.
2) Remove the support of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, from the fan disk flange.
3) Remove the tube of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, from the center vent tube [11].
(r) Install the retaining ring [12] onto the LPT shaft [10].
(s) Remove the protective ring, SPL-6183, from the fan disk hole.
(t) Do a visual inspection to make sure of the correct installation of retaining ring [12].

H. LPT Shaft-Plug O-ring Replacement
SUBTASK 72-55-00-020-004-F00
WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENTS OF THE OIL SYSTEM IF THE ENGINE
IS HOT. THESE COMPONENTS STAY HOTTER THAN OTHER
COMPONENTS. HOT COMPONENTS CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT OPEN THE OIL SYSTEM UNTIL THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO.
THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES AFTER AN
ENGINE STOPS. A PRESSURIZED OIL SYSTEM CAN RELEASE A SPRAY OF
HOT OIL THAT CAN BURN YOU.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(WARNING PRECEDES)
WARNING
DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON YOU. PUT ON CLOTHES, GOGGLES, AND
OTHER EQUIPMENT FOR PROTECTION, OR LET THE ENGINE BECOME
COOL. HOT OIL CAN BURN YOU.
CAUTION
DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON THE ENGINE OR OTHER COMPONENTS.
IMMEDIATELY CLEAN THE COMPONENT IF OIL FALLS ON IT. OIL CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO PAINT AND RUBBER.
(1) Do these steps to replace the LPT shaft plug O-ring [23] and O-ring [24].
(a) Install the protective ring, SPL-6183, in position in the fan disk hole.
(b) Remove the retaining ring [22] from forward end of the LPT shaft [20], with a scribe.
(c) Do these steps to install the pusher/puller, SPL-6182:
1) Screw the tube of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, into the LPT shaft plug [21].
2) Install the support of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, on the fan disk flange with
screws.
3) Engage the plate of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, in the slot of the screw and attach
it with the knurled nut.
(d) Do these steps to remove the LPT shaft plug [21]:
1) Manually turn clockwise the screw of fixture of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, to
disengage the LPT shaft plug [21] from the LPT shaft [20].
NOTE: You can use a wrench if the counter torque is important.
2) Remove the support of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, from the fan disk flange.
3) Remove the LPT shaft plug [21] equipped with the tube of the pusher/puller,
SPL-6182, from the LPT shaft [20].
4) Remove the tube of the pusher/puller, SPL-6182, from the LPT shaft plug [21].
(e) Remove and discard O-ring [23] and O-ring [24] located in the forward/aft grooves of the
LPT shaft plug [21].
WARNING
ACETONE IS AN AGENT THAT IS FLAMMABLE, EXPLOSIVE,
POISONOUS, AND AN IRRITANT. MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS OBEY ALL
OF THE PRECAUTIONS WHEN ACETONE IS USED.
• GAS/AIR MIXTURES MORE THAN THE LOWER EXPLOSIVE LIMIT
(LEL) CAN CAUSE AN EXPLOSION IF HIGH HEAT, SPARKS, OR
FLAMES SUPPLY IGNITION.
• USE IN AN AREA OPEN TO THE AIR.
• CLOSE THE CONTAINER WHEN NOT USED.
• DO NOT GET ACETONE IN THE EYES, ON THE SKIN, OR ON YOUR
CLOTHES.
• DO NOT BREATHE THE GAS.
(f) Clean the oil stains on the plug grooves with acetone solvent, E50001.
(g) Install the LPT shaft plug [21] in the storage box.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
WARNING
DO NOT LET THE ENGINE OIL STAY ON YOUR SKIN. ENGINE OIL IS
POISONOUS. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES. USE ENGINE OIL IN AN
AREA WITH GOOD AIRFLOW. DO NOT GET ENGINE OIL ON YOUR
CLOTHES OR ON THE AIRPLANE. ENGINE OIL CAN CAUSE INJURIES.
(h) Lightly coat new O-ring [23] and new O-ring [24] with oil, D00599 [CP2442].
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU CORRECTLY INSTALL NEW O-RING IN THE
SEAL GROOVES AT THE FORWARD END AND THE AFT END OF THE
LPT SHAFT-PLUG. IF THE O-RING IS NOT CORRECTLY INSTALLED,
DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE CAN OCCUR.
(i) Install the new O-ring [23] and new O-ring [24] into the seal grooves of the LPT shaft
plug [21].
(j) Install the LPT shaft plug [21] assembly into the forward end of the LPT shaft [20] and
onto the CVT.
NOTE: Insert the lug of the LPT shaft plug in aligned slots of the LPT coupling nut and
the LPT shaft.
(k) Install the retaining ring [22] onto the LPT shaft [20].
(l) Remove the protective ring, SPL-6183, in position in the fan disk hole.
(m) Do a visual inspection to make sure the correct installation of the retaining ring [22].

(1) Examine the air/oil separator as follows:
(a) Examine all areas that you can see for:
1) Corrosion or pitting
a) All quantities permitted.

a) Not permitted.
SUBTASK 72-55-00-900-001-F00
(2) If you find cracks, replace the air/oil separator, unless you are given other instructions
(TASK 72-56-01-000-801-F00 and TASK 72-56-01-400-801-F00).
SUBTASK 72-55-00-211-001-F00
(3) Examine the seal teeth of the center vent tube rear extension duct.
(a) Seizure marks, scratches, nicks and dents.
1) Permitted, if the depth is not more than of 0.003 in. (0.076 mm).
(b) Bent seal tooth
1) All quantities permitted, if the cumulative length of the bent tooth is not more than
1/12 of the circumference.
(c) High metal
1) Not permitted.
(d) Waviness
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) All quantities permitted, if the amplitude of indication is not more than 0.015 in.
(0.381 mm).
2) Cracks are not permitted.
(e) Crack or missing (worn away)
1) Not permitted.
(f) Worn outer diameter
1) All quantities permitted, if the seal tooth outer diameter is between 2.077 in.
(52.756 mm) and 2.079 in. (52.807 mm).

(5) Do these steps to remove the oil inlet cover [9]:
CAUTION
USE TWO WRENCHES TO LOOSEN THE TUBE COUPLING NUTS. USE
ONE WRENCH TO HOLD THE MATING PART, AND THE OTHER TO
LOOSEN THE COUPLING NUT. IF YOU DO NOT USE TWO WRENCHES,
DAMAGE TO THE TUBES AND MATING PART CAN OCCUR.
(a) Remove the damping oil tube [12].
(b) Remove the oil supply tube [11].

support.
2) Install the oil inlet cover puller adapter, SPL-8854, on the rear face of the oil inlet
cover [9].
3) Use the puller to remove the oil inlet cover [9].
4) Remove the oil inlet cover puller adapter, SPL-8854, from the oil inlet cover [9].
(d) Remove the O-ring [7] and gasket seal [6].
1) Discard the O-ring [7] and gasket seal [6].
(e) If it is necessary, examine and clean the sump area to make sure that there is no
unwanted material.
NOTE: When you remove the oil inlet cover, some pieces of gasket seal may detach and
fall into the sump.
1) Make sure that the sump is free of any unwanted material.
(f) Clean the mating faces of the oil inlet cover [9].
(g) Remove the nipple [10] and the O-ring [13] from the oil inlet cover [9].
1) Discard the O-ring [13].
(h) Remove the nipple [20] and the O-ring [21] from the rear face of No. 5 bearing support.
1) Discard the O-ring [21].

G. Turbine Rear Frame (TRF) Oil Inlet Cover Installation
SUBTASK 72-56-00-420-001-F00
(1) Do these steps to install the oil inlet cover [9]:
(a) Install the oil nipple [20] on the rear face of No. 5 bearing support.
1) Lubricate a new O-ring [21] with oil, D00623 [CP5066].
2) Install the O-ring [21] on the nipple [20].
3) Install the nipple [20] on the rear face of the No. 5 bearing support.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) Tighten the nipple [20] manually to seat.
b) Tighten the nipple [20] to 90 in-lb (10.2 N·m) - 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m).
(b) Lubricate a new O-ring [7] with vaseline, D00672 [CP5070].
(c) Install the O-ring [7] on the oil inlet cover [9].
(d) Install a new gasket seal [6], on the No. 5 bearing support.
1) Use guide pin, SPL-14685, to hold the gasket seal [6] until the oil inlet cover [9] is
attached.
(e) Install the oil inlet cover puller adapter, SPL-8854, on the rear flange of the oil inlet
cover [9].
(f) Install the oil inlet cover [9] with the oil inlet cover puller adapter, SPL-8854, on the No. 5
bearing support.
1) Match the position of the cover flange with the oil supply and scavenge tube [5] that
comes out at the bottom of the No. 5 bearing support.
(g) Apply a thin layer of graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101], on the threads of the
twelve bolts [8].
(h) Install the twelve bolts [8] that attach the oil inlet cover [9] to the No. 5 bearing support.
1) Tighten the bolts [8] manually.
(i) With hand pressure on oil inlet cover [9], use a slide hammer, COM-13625, on oil inlet
cover puller adapter, SPL-8854, or a non-metallic mallet, STD-583, to install the oil inlet
cover flange against the No. 5 bearing support.
(j) Remove the oil inlet cover puller adapter, SPL-8854, from the oil inlet cover [9].
(k) Initially, tighten the bolts [8] to 35 in-lb (4 N·m) in a criss-cross pattern, for correct
installation of the O-ring [7] (Figure 402).
(l) Tighten the bolts [8] to 70 in-lb (8 N·m) in a criss-cross pattern (Figure 402).
(m) Tighten the bolts [8] to 110.0 in-lb (12.4 N·m) - 120.0 in-lb (13.6 N·m) in a criss-cross
pattern (Figure 402).
(n) Wait for 5 minutes minimum.
(o) Loosen all bolts [8] by approximately 180°.
(p) Tighten the bolts [8] to 110.0 in-lb (12.4 N·m) - 120.0 in-lb (13.6 N·m) in a criss-cross
pattern (Figure 402).
(q) Wait for 5 minutes minimum.
(r) Loosen all bolts [8] by approximately 180°.
(s) Tighten the bolts [8] to 110.0 in-lb (12.4 N·m) - 120.0 in-lb (13.6 N·m) in a criss-cross
pattern (Figure 402).
(t) Tighten the bolts [8] to 110.0 in-lb (12.4 N·m) - 120.0 in-lb (13.6 N·m) starting with bolt
No. 1 clockwise.
(u) Do these steps to install the nipple [10] on the oil inlet cover [9]:
1) Lubricate a new O-ring [13] with oil, D00623 [CP5066].
2) Install the O-ring [13] on the nipple [10].
3) Install the nipple [10] on the oil inlet cover [9].
a) Tighten the nipple [10] manually to seat.
b) Tighten the nipple [10] to 180.0 in-lb (20 N·m) - 195.0 in-lb (22.0 N·m).
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

ENGINE OIL IS POISONOUS. USE PROTECTION EQUIPMENT IN AN

(a) Lubricate threads of the nipple [10], nipple [20] and nuts (rear flange of the nozzle) of the
oil supply tube [11] and damping oil tube [12] with engine oil, D00599 [CP2442].
(b) Put the oil supply tube [11] and damping oil tube [12] in their installation position as
follows:
1) Connect the damping oil tube [12] to the nipple [20] of the No. 5 bearing support.
a) Tighten the coupling nut by hand.
2) Connect the damping oil tube [12] to the oil supply tube [11].
a) Tighten the coupling nut by hand.
3) Connect the oil supply tube [11] to the nipple [10].
a) Tighten the coupling nut by hand.
(c) Loosen the oil supply tube [19] and rear sump oil supply tube brackets to have flexibility
for connection with the oil supply tube [11].
(d) Connect the oil supply tube [11] to the oil supply tube [19].
1) Tighten the coupling nut by hand.
(e) Tighten, without applying the final torque, the oil supply tube [11] to the nipple [10].
(f) Tighten, without applying the final torque, the oil supply tube [19] to the oil supply
tube [11].
(g) Tighten, without applying the final torque, the oil supply tube [19] and rear sump oil
supply tube to stiffen it (TASK 72-56-00-300-801-F00).
(h) Make sure that the oil supply tube [19] is not in contact with the inside of the TRF strut.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU USE THE SOFT NOSE PLIERS WHEN YOU
TORQUE THE UNION NUT. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE
TUBES CAN OCCUR.
(i) Hold the damping oil tube [12] with the soft jaws pliers, STD-26254.

tube [12].
(k) Tighten, without applying the final torque, the union nut of the damping oil tube [12]
connected to the nipple [20] of the No. 5 bearing support.
(l) Make sure that the oil supply tube [11] and damping oil tube [12] are installed without
strain.

(m) Hold the nipple [10] with the wrench, STD-3724.

265.0 in-lb (29.9 N·m) - 300.0 in-lb (33.9 N·m).

265.0 in-lb (29.9 N·m) - 300.0 in-lb (33.9 N·m).
(q) Do these steps to check the Dim. A (Figure 403):
1) Do a check of Dim. A in four equally spaced locations.
NOTE: The tightening step must not cause the oil supply line to move.
a) Make sure that the Dim. A is minimum 0.078 in. (2.0 mm).
2) If the Dim. A criterion is less than 0.078 in. (2.0 mm), do these steps:
a) Do a visual inspection of the oil supply tube [19].
b) Do a torque check of the two coupling nuts of the oil supply tube [19].
c) Disconnect the oil supply tube [19].
d) Install the oil supply tube [19] again to get Dim. A within the minimum criterion
of 0.078 in. (2.0 mm).
3) Make sure that there is no perforation in the insulation blanket of the oil supply
tube [19].
4) If the Dim. A criterion stays less than 0.078 in. (2.0 mm) or if there is perforation in
the insulation blanket, replace the oil supply tube [19]
(TASK 72-56-00-300-801-F00).
(r) Make sure that the oil supply tube [19] is not in contact with the inside of the TRF strut.
(s) Tighten the oil supply tube [19] to the rear sump oil supply tube and brackets
(TASK 72-56-00-300-801-F00).
(t) To tighten the damping oil tube [12], do these steps:

MAKE SURE THAT YOU USE THE SOFT NOSE PLIERS WHEN YOU

1) Hold the damping oil tube [12] with the soft jaws pliers, STD-26254.

tube [11] to 90.0 in-lb (10.2 N·m) - 100.0 in-lb (11.3 N·m).
3) Tighten the union nut of the damping oil tube [12] connected to the nipple [20] of the
No. 5 bearing support to 90.0 in-lb (10.2 N·m) - 100.0 in-lb (11.3 N·m).
(u) Install safety wire, G02345 [CP8001], or safety wire, G02495 [CP8002], on the coupling

nuts of the damping oil tube [12].

E. Turbine Frame Assembly Inspection
SUBTASK 72-56-00-200-001-F00
(1) Examine the forward outer flange and the aft outer flange for damage:
(a) Cracks that connect the bolt holes
1) Not permitted.
2) A continue-in-service limit of 10 cycles is permitted for one crack that connects two
bolt holes.
(b) Cracks that extend from the bolt holes to the outer edge of the flange
1) One crack 0.20 in. (5.1 mm) in length from a bolt hole is permitted, with this limit:
a) There is a minimum separation of five holes between cracks.
(c) Cracks that extend from the bolt holes to the casing skin
1) Five axial cracks 0.20 in. (5.1 mm) in length on each flange are permitted with this
limit:
a) There is a minimum separation of 10 holes between cracks.
2) No circumferential cracks are permitted.
(d) Cracks in other areas of the flange
1) Five cracks on each flange 0.20 in. (5.1 mm) in length are permitted with this limit:
a) There is a minimum separation of 5.0 in. (127 mm) between all other cracks.
(e) Nicks, scores and scratches
1) All damage is permitted with these limits:
a) It is permitted to have five nicks, scores or scratches that are not more than
1.0 in. (25.4 mm) long on each flange.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
b) Damage is not more than 0.020 in. (0.51 mm) in depth after you remove the
high metal. Refer to General Removal of High Metal
(TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00).
c) There is a minimum separation of 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) between each nick, score
or scratch.
SUBTASK 72-56-00-200-002-F00
(2) Examine the engine mounting lug area and strut attach points for this damage:
NOTE: Includes the adjacent welds and those heat affected areas.
(a) Cracks that extend from the bolt holes
1) Not permitted.
2) A continue-in-service limit of 10 cycles is permitted for one crack that goes out of
one mounting lug bolt hole and is not more than 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) in length.
(b) Cracks in the areas of the engine mounting lugs (includes the welds):
1) Not permitted.
2) A continue-in-service limit of 10 cycles is permitted for one crack that is not more
than 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) in length.
(c) Nicks, scores and scratches
1) There is no limit to the number of nicks, scores, and scratches which are permitted
with these conditions:
a) Not more than 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) in length.
b) Not more than 0.020 in. (0.51 mm) in depth, after you remove the high metal.
Refer to General Removal of High Metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00).
c) Minimum separation of 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) between each nick, score, or scratch.
SUBTASK 72-56-00-200-003-F00
(3) Examine all other areas of outer casing skin for damage:
(a) Cracks
1) Not permitted.
2) A continue-in-service limit of 10 cycles is permitted for one crack that is not more
than 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) in length.
(b) Nicks, scores, and scratches
1) There is no limit to the number of nicks, scores, and scratches which are permitted
with these conditions:
a) Not more than 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) in length.
b) Not more than 0.020 in. (0.51 mm) in depth, after you remove the high metal.
Refer to General Removal of High Metal (Hand Blending - Maintenance
Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00).
c) Minimum separation of 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) between each nick, score, or scratch.
SUBTASK 72-56-00-200-004-F00
(4) Examine the oil supply and scavenge tubes for damage:
(a) Cracks
1) Not permitted.
(b) Nicks, scores, and scratches
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) There is no limit to the number of nicks, scores, and scratches if each is not more
than 0.01 in. (0.25 mm) in depth after you remove the high metal. Refer to General
Removal of High Metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00).
(c) Dents
1) Two dents for each tube are permitted if they have a smooth contour and are not
more than 0.05 in. (1.27 mm) in depth.
(d) Oil leakage and coking
1) With the engine stopped, a Continue-In-Service (CIS) limit of 50 cycles is permitted
for oil coking or oil wetting on oil scavenge tube, only if you do a daily inspection to
check that drain holes are not blocked.
SUBTASK 72-56-00-200-005-F00
(5) Examine the struts for damage:
(a) Cracks in the parent metal
1) Not permitted.
(b) Cracks in the welds
1) Not permitted.
(c) Nicks, scores, and scratches
1) There is no limit to the number of nicks, scores, and scratches with no limit to
length, with this condition:
a) Not more than 0.02 in. (0.51 mm) in depth after you remove the high metal.
Refer to General Removal of High Metal (TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00).
(d) Dents
1) There is no limit to the number of dents with a maximum depth of 0.02 in.
(0.51 mm), if they have a smooth contour.
(e) Oil mark on the No. 7 strut
1) Oil marks are permitted.

(b) Mechanical cleaning
NOTE: This is a mechanical cleaning because the tube is non-removable.
1) Put protection on the No. 5 bearing to prevent any contamination by the material.
NOTE: Be careful to put protection equipment on the No. 5 bearing before you start
a mechanical cleaning of oil supply line.
2) Put protection on all the cavities and tube ends to prevent any contamination by the
material.
3) Put a cap for the oil supply tube on the outer case side.
4) Put a sufficient quantity of WD-40 lubricant, D00139, penetrant corrosion inhibitor
compound, C00174 to fill the tube and keep it to get effect on coking in the
concerned area for a sufficient time.
5) Put a container under the tube to collect the penetrant corrosion inhibitor.
6) Remove the cap from the tube and collect the penetrant corrosion inhibitor.
7) Turn the tube in its position to get access to the ends of tube.
8) Introduce a cylinder-brush tool through the tube ends and move the tool to the
coked area.
9) Put a small quantity of kerosene, G50611 [CP1065] or aviation turbine fuel, G51056
with a filler tool in the tube.
NOTE: Do not permit the kerosene to touch your skin or clothes. Remove your
clothes if the fuel touches them. Rinse your skin fully with water where the
fuel touched you. Fuel can burn your skin.
Kerosene is flammable, an irritant, an allergen, and has poisonous
deterioration. Use personal protection equipment. Use vapor/fume control
or respirator.
10) Do an alternative movement of rotation on the tool to break the coking
contamination.
11) Extract the tool and use lint-free cloths to collect the coked particles.
12) Clean the cylinder-brush tool with kerosene, G50611 [CP1065] or aviation turbine
fuel, G51056.
a) Repeat the cleaning until tube is free of particles/contamination.
NOTE: No oil coked particles/contamination is permitted.
NOTE: Be careful to not introduce any particles/contamination to the internal
side of bearing support to prevent bearing contamination. If not, you
can cause damage to engine.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)

 ALL
 ALL PRE SB CFM56-7B-72-339 AND PRE SB 737-CFM56-7B-72-0169 AND PRE SB
737-CFM56-7B-72-0254 (Continued)

[CP1041] or aviation turbine fuel, G51056.

H. Cleaning Internal Lube Oil Tubes
SUBTASK 72-56-00-110-014-F00
(1) This cleaning method is effective for removal of coke from internal lube oil tubes where the
tubes can be disconnected to permit flow through or plugged to permit a douche type of
flushing. This solution is not to enter sumps or lube system components which cannot be
thoroughly flushed and purged.
(a) Attach the steel tubing and a suitable pump to the lube tube to be cleaned, to supply
cleaning solution to the tube and return it to the heated cleaning bath, STD-6552.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
THIS CLEANING SOLUTION IS STRONGLY ALKALINE. VENT AREA AND
WEAR FACE SHIELD AND PROTECTIVE CLOTHING. IF SOLUTION
CONTACTS THE SKIN OR EYES, FLUSH EXPOSED AREAS
THOROUGHLY WITH COOL WATER AND SEEK IMMEDIATE MEDICAL
AID.
(b) Pump alkaline permanganate, G51456 [S1001, S1012, S1014, S1192, S1231, S1235] or
alkaline rust remover, G51455 [S1218] through the tube and back into the heated
cleaning bath, STD-6552 for 3 hours maximum. Soaking time is a function of the coke
thickness.
NOTE: Solution flow rate is not critical but should be sufficient to maintain tube and
cleaning solution operating temperature. Tubing may be rigid or flexible, however,
length should be as short as possible to reduce heat losses. The pump packing
should be non-oxidizable material such as Teflon.
(c) After cleaning, disconnect the lines and drain tube. Flush the tube with cold tap water
until distinctive color of cleaning solution disappears.
CAUTION
DO NOT MIX CLEANING AGENT AND STAIN REMOVER. KEEP TANKS
SEPARATED OR DAMAGE CAN OCCUR.
(d) To remove the cleaning solution stain on the internal surface of the tube when using one
of the alkaline permanganate, G51456 [S1001, S1012, S1014, S1192, S1231, S1235]
solutions, pump solution of oxalic acid, B50041 [C04-099] through the tube for 2 or 3
minutes at room temperature.
NOTE: Hoses may be used with the stain remover solution. Various plastics and
elastomers are compatible with this material.
(e) Disconnect the lines and drain tube. Flush with the cold tap water until the effluent water
has the same acidity as the inlet water (use indicator paper).
(f) Disconnect the lines, drain tube and dry with clean shop air.
(g) Procedure may be repeated.

4. Oil Scavenge Line Cleaning
(Figure 704)
A. General
(1) This task give the instructions to clean coking deposits from the rear sump oil scavenge line
and related parts.
(a) The scavenge line includes the rear sump scavenge tube installed through the No. 7
turbine frame strut, the rear sump oil scavenge tube and the No. 5 bearing support
nipple.
(b) The scavenge tube installed through the No. 7 strut is not removable, do a mechanical
cleaning of the scavenge tube (not removed).
(c) The rear sump oil scavenge tube is removable, if it is necessary, do a chemical cleaning
of the removed tube.
(2) It is necessary to remove the oil inlet cover to do this task.

(5) Do these steps to degrease and mechanically clean the oil scavenge tube (not removable):

CAUTION

(a) Put protection on the No. 5 bearing to prevent any contamination by the material.
(b) Put protection on all the cavities and tube ends to prevent any contamination by the
material.

(d) Put a sufficient quantity of WD-40 lubricant, D00139 (CP2554), to fill the tube and keep it

(f) Remove the cap from the tube and collect the penetrant corrosion inhibitor.
(g) Turn the tube in its position to get access to the ends of tube.

area.
(i) Put a small quantity of kerosene, G50611 [CP1065], or aviation turbine fuel, G51056, with
a filler tool in the tube.
(j) Do an alternative movement of rotation on the tool to break the coking contamination.
(k) Extract the tool and use lint-free cloths to collect the coked particle.

2. Oil Supply Tube Replacement
(Figure 801)
A. General
(1) This task is for Configuration 1 Post-CFMI-SB 72-0339 Engines that have non-symmetrical
(twisted) struts and Configuration 2 that have symmetrical struts and straight tubes on the
Turbine Rear Frame (TRF).
(a) The oil supply tube is installed in strut No. 10 of the TRF.
(b) The oil supply tube has a removable retaining ring.
(2) Do this task if the oil flow through the oil supply tube is blocked by oil coking.

A. General
(1) This procedure is for Engines Post-CFMI-SB 72-0169 or Post-CFMI-SB 72-0254 or
Post-CFMI- SB 72-0676, which have symmetrical struts on the Turbine Rear Frame (TRF).

turbine frame only on wing, or on Low Pressure Turbine (LPT) major module.

WARNING

 ALL
3) Complete the removal of the remaining tack weld material with a small manual
grinding tool and grind the tack weld beads to have a continuous surface with the
adjacent areas. Refer to TASK 70-41-12 (70-41-12, Power Blending) CFM Standard
Practices Manual.
WARNING
USE EYE PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COMPRESSED AIR TO

a) Use S2 sensitivity.
b) Cracks are not permitted.
(c) Do an inspection of the tapped hole with a gage.
1) Indications are not permitted.
2) If there is any indication in the tapped hole, this repair is not applicable to the part.
(d) Install the new studs as follows:
1) Apply a thin layer of graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101] on the stud
threads which go into the hole of the frame.
2) Tighten the new stud as follows:
a) Screw the new stud by hand on the turbine frame.
b) Tighten with the wrench to complete the installation. Refer to TASK 70-70-11
(70-70-11, Tightening Methods) CFM Standard Practices Manual.
c) Torque the stud to 925 in-lb (104.5 N·m)-1022 in-lb (115.5 N·m).
d) Loosen the stud.
e) Torque the stud a second time to 925 in-lb (104.5 N·m)-1022 in-lb (115.5 N·m).
WARNING
METAL PARTICLES FROM MACHINING CAN CAUSE DAMAGE, INJURY,
OR IRRITATION TO YOU. USE PERSONAL PROTECTION EQUIPMENT.

General) CFM Standard Practices Manual (Figure 807).
NOTE: The pin must be machined in relation to the pin hole to have a tightening of

rear extension duct [8] as follows:
1) Engage the air/oil separator slots with the center vent tube lugs.

NOTE: Engage the air/oil separator offset slot with the center vent tube offset lug.
The air/oil separator offset slot and center vent tube offset lug have
spherical indentation for identification.
3) Make sure that you fully seat the air/oil separator [1].
(h) Measure Dimension C.
1) Do this measurement at four equally-spaced locations and calculate the average of
the four measurements.

(j) If the difference between the calculated dimension C and the actual dimension C is more
than 0.003 inch (0.075 mm), do these steps:
1) Remove the parts.
2) Find the cause for the difference.

(1) To remove the magnetic seal [1], do these steps (Figure 202):

3) Operate the impact puller to remove the rotating ring.
4) Remove the rotating ring from the pusher/puller.
a) Loosen the pusher/puller nut and screw.
b) Remove and discard the O-ring [3].

F. Install the Magnetic Seal
SUBTASK 72-60-00-410-001-F00
CAUTION
USE CLEAN, LINT-FREE GLOVES WHEN YOU TOUCH THE MAGNETIC
SEALS. THIS WILL PREVENT CONTAMINATION.
CAUTION
REPLACE ALL OF THE SEAL, IF YOU CAUSED DAMAGE TO A COMPONENT
OF THE SEAL. MAGNETIC SEALS ARE MATCHED ASSEMBLIES. IF YOU MIX
COMPONENTS, OIL LEAKAGE COULD OCCUR.
(1) Do these steps to install the magnetic seal [1]:
(a) Install the new O-ring [2] and O-ring [3]:
1) Apply a light layer of clean oil, D00599 [CP2442] on the O-rings.
2) Install the new O-ring [2] on the seal housing assembly (OD).
3) Install the new O-ring [3] on the rotating ring (ID).
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THE POLISHED FACE OF THE SEAL CASE AND THE
CARBON FACE OF THE ROTATING RING ARE CLEAN. LEAKS WILL
RESULT IF PARTICLES, EVEN OF A VERY SMALL SIZE, ARE BETWEEN
THESE PARTS DURING THE INSTALLATION.
(b) Apply a layer of clean oil, D00599 [CP2442] to the carbon seal face of the rotating ring
and the polished face of the seal case.
(c) Carefully install the rotating ring on the seal housing assembly:
1) Make sure the carbon seal touches the polished surface of the seal case.
2) Align the rotating ring with the internal diameter of the seal housing assembly.
(d) Apply a light layer of clean oil, D00599 [CP2442] to the bearing surface of the gear shaft
that will touch the rotating ring and the O-ring.
CAUTION
DO NOT HIT THE MAGNETIC SEAL INTO THE GEARBOX RECESS. THE
ROTATING RING AND SEAL HOUSING ASSEMBLY CAN MOVE APART
AND THE CARBON SEAL CAN BE DAMAGED.
CAUTION
INSTALL THE ROTATING RING AND THE SEAL HOUSING ASSEMBLY
TOGETHER ONTO THE GEAR SHAFT, UNTIL THE SEAL HOUSING
ASSEMBLY TOUCHES THE GEARBOX. DO NOT SEPARATELY SLIDE
THE ROTATING PART OF THE SEAL ONTO THE SHAFT. IF YOU INSTALL
THE ROTATING RING AND SEAL HOUSING ASSEMBLY SEPARATELY,
OIL LEAKAGE COULD OCCUR.
(e) Put the magnetic seal on the gear shaft.
1) Make sure the outer O-ring of the seal housing assembly touches the gearbox
bearing housing.
(f) Apply a light layer of graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101] to the three gearbox
studs.
(g) Install the nuts and washers on the studs:
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)

 ALL
1) Tighten the nuts with your fingers.
2) Make sure the washers touch the seal housing assembly.
(h) Tighten the nuts in a sequence until the seal housing assembly moves fully into its
position in contact with the gearbox housing.
(i) Tighten the nuts to 29.2-32.7 pound-inches (3.3-3.7 Newton meters).

CAUTION

(2) Do these steps to install the sealol seal [11] (Except N2 Drive Pad):
(a) Install the new O-rings:
1) Apply a light layer of clean oil, D00599 [CP2442], on the O-rings.
2) Install the new O-ring [12] in the grooves on the seal housing assembly (OD).
3) Install the new O-ring [13] or the new O-ring [14] in the grooves on the rotating ring
(ID).
(b) Apply a light layer of clean oil, D00599 [CP2442], on bearing surfaces of the gear shaft:
1) Apply the oil on the bearing surfaces of the gear shaft which will touch the O-ring on
the rotating ring.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE POLISHED FACE OF THE ROTATING RING AND
THE CARBON FACE OF THE SEAL HOUSING ARE CLEAN. LEAKS WILL
OCCUR IF SMALL PARTICLES ARE BETWEEN THESE PARTS WHEN
YOU INSTALL THEM.
(c) Apply a layer of clean oil, D00599 [CP2442] to the carbon seal face of the seal housing
assembly.
(d) Install the rotating ring on the gear shaft with the pusher/puller, SPL-10797, or the
pusher/puller, SPL-2191 (Figure 203):
1) Loosen the pusher/puller nut and screw.
2) Put the rotating ring on the tool and against the sleeve.
3) Tighten the pusher/puller screw, then tighten the pusher/puller nut to make sure the
rotating ring will not turn in the sleeve.
4) Install the rotating ring on the gear shaft:
a) Turn the pusher/puller, with the handle, until the slots in the rotating ring align
with the lugs in the bearing.
b) Turn the pusher/puller in each direction to make sure the rotating ring slots are
engaged with the bearing lugs.
5) Loosen the pusher/puller screw and nut.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
6) Remove the tool.
CAUTION
DO NOT TAP THE SEALOL SEAL INTO THE GEARBOX RECESS. THE
ROTATING RING AND SEAL CASE CAN MOVE APART AND CAUSE
DAMAGE TO THE CARBON SEAL.
(e) Put the seal housing assembly on the gear shaft (Figure 204).
1) Make sure the outer O-ring of the seal housing assembly touches the gearbox
bearing housing.
(f) Apply a light layer of graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101], to the three gearbox
studs.
(g) Install the nuts and washers on the studs:
1) Tighten the nuts with your fingers.
2) Make sure the washers touch the seal housing assembly.
(h) Tighten the nuts in a sequence until the seal housing goes fully into its position in contact
with the gearbox housing assembly.
(i) Torque the nuts to 29.2-32.7 pound-inches (3.3-3.7 Newton meters).

72-60-00-200-801-F00Accessory Gearbox and Transfer Gearbox Mount InspectionPDF p. 1337
2. Accessory Gearbox and Transfer Gearbox Mount Inspection
(Figure 601 and Figure 602)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) This is a visual check of the mounts on the transfer gearbox (TGB) housing and the accessory
gearbox housing (AGB).
(2) The AGB is on the left side of the fan case and the TGB is at the 9:00 o'clock position on the
fan frame.
B. References
Reference Title
71-00-02-000-801-F00 Power Plant - Removal (P/B 401)
71-00-02-400-801-F00 Power Plant - Installation (P/B 401)
71-11-02-010-801-F00 Open the Fan Cowl Panels (P/B 201)
71-11-02-410-801-F00 Close the Fan Cowl Panels (P/B 201)
72-62-00-000-801-F00 Transfer Gearbox Assembly Removal (P/B 401)
72-62-00-400-801-F00 Transfer Gearbox Assembly Installation (P/B 401)

Zone Area
411 Engine 1 - Engine
421 Engine 2 - Engine
D. Procedure
SUBTASK 72-60-00-210-001-F00
(1) Do this task: Open the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-010-801-F00.
SUBTASK 72-60-00-210-002-F00
(2) Do a visual check of the AGB clevis mounts for damage (Figure 601):
(a) If you find damage that is more than the limits, replace the engine, unless you are given
other instructions.
These are the tasks:
Power Plant - Removal, TASK 71-00-02-000-801-F00,
Power Plant - Installation, TASK 71-00-02-400-801-F00.
(b) Cracks
1) Not serviceable.
(c) Loose bushing in the clevis mounts
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Not permitted.
(d) Loose mount pin
1) Not permitted.
a) Tighten the mount pin if it is loose.
SUBTASK 72-60-00-210-003-F00
(3) Do a visual check of the TGB mounts for damage (Figure 602):
(a) If you find damage that is more than the limits, replace the TGB, unless you are given
other instructions.
These are the tasks:
Transfer Gearbox Assembly Removal, TASK 72-62-00-000-801-F00,
Transfer Gearbox Assembly Installation, TASK 72-62-00-400-801-F00.
(b) Cracks
1) Not serviceable.
(c) Loose attachment bolts
1) Not permitted.
a) Tighten the attachment nut (TASK 72-62-00-400-801-F00).
SUBTASK 72-60-00-210-004-F00
(4) Do this task: Close the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-410-801-F00.
72-60-00-200-802-F00Accessory Gearbox, Transfer Gearbox, and Horizontal Drive Shaft - Oil Leakage InspectionPDF p. 1341
3. Accessory Gearbox, Transfer Gearbox, and Horizontal Drive Shaft - Oil Leakage Inspection
A. General
(1) This is a visual check for oil leaks from the transfer gearbox (TGB) housing, the accessory
gearbox housing (AGB) and the horizontal drive shaft housing (HDS).
(2) The AGB is on the left side of the fan case and the TGB is at the 9:00 o'clock position on the
fan frame.
(3) The HDS housing is between the AGB and the TGB.
B. References
Reference Title
71-11-02-010-801-F00 Open the Fan Cowl Panels (P/B 201)
71-11-02-410-801-F00 Close the Fan Cowl Panels (P/B 201)
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
411 Engine 1 - Engine
421 Engine 2 - Engine
D. Procedure
SUBTASK 72-60-00-010-009-F00
(1) Do this task: Open the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-010-801-F00.
SUBTASK 72-60-00-210-005-F00
(2) Do a visual check of the AGB for oil leakage.
SUBTASK 72-60-00-210-006-F00
(3) Do a visual check of the TGB for oil leakage.
SUBTASK 72-60-00-210-007-F00
(4) Do a visual check of the HDS housing for oil leakage.
SUBTASK 72-60-00-900-001-F00
(5) If you find evidence of oil leakage, repair or replace components as it is necessary to stop the
leakage.
SUBTASK 72-60-00-410-006-F00
(6) Do this task: Close the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-410-801-F00.

H. Replacement of the 32-tooth bevel gear oil nozzle O-rings
SUBTASK 72-62-00-960-001-F00
WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENTS OF THE OIL SYSTEM IF THE ENGINE
IS HOT. THESE COMPONENTS STAY HOTTER THAN OTHER
COMPONENTS. HOT COMPONENTS CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT OPEN THE OIL SYSTEM UNTIL THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO.
THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES AFTER AN
ENGINE STOPS. A PRESSURIZED OIL SYSTEM CAN RELEASE A SPRAY OF
HOT OIL THAT CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON YOU. PUT ON CLOTHES, GOGGLES, AND
OTHER EQUIPMENT FOR PROTECTION, OR LET THE ENGINE BECOME
COOL. HOT OIL CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON THE ENGINE OR OTHER COMPONENTS.
IMMEDIATELY CLEAN THE COMPONENT IF OIL FALLS ON IT. OIL CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO PAINT AND RUBBER.
WARNING
ENGINE OIL IS POISONOUS. USE PROTECTION EQUIPMENT IN AN AREA
WITH GOOD AIR FLOW TO AVOID INJURY.
(1) Do these steps to replace the 32-tooth bevel gear oil nozzle o-ring [1] and o-ring [2]
(Figure 201, Figure 202).
(a) Remove the bolt [3] which attaches the oil nozzle plug [4] to the transfer gearbox (TGB)
housing.
(b) Remove the plug [4] with the inner adapter P30 [5] of the puller adapters, SPL-6180 and
impact puller [6].
(c) Remove the inner adapter P30 [5] of the puller adapter, SPL-6180.
(d) Remove and discard the o-ring [7].
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(e) Remove the oil nozzle [8] with the inner adapter P32 [9] of the puller adapter, SPL-6180,
and an impact puller [6].
(f) Remove the inner adapter P32 [9] of the puller adapter, SPL-6180.
(g) Remove and discard o-ring [1] and o-ring [2].
WARNING
MAKE SURE TO PREVENT ACETONE CONTACT WITH SKIN. ACETONE
IRRITATES SKIN AND IS EXPLOSIVE. USE FUME CONTROL OR USE A
RESPIRATOR TO PREVENT INJURY.
(h) Clean the oil nozzle [8] with acetone solvent, B01058 [CP1039].
WARNING
ENGINE OIL IS POISONOUS. USE PROTECTION EQUIPMENT IN AN
AREA WITH GOOD AIR FLOW TO AVOID INJURY.
(i) Apply a layer of engine oil, D00599 [CP2442] on the new o-ring [1] and o-ring [2].
(j) Use the seal fittings tool set, SPL-9874 to install the new o-ring [1] on the oil nozzle [8]
then manually install the new o-ring [2].
WARNING
ENGINE OIL IS POISONOUS. USE PROTECTION EQUIPMENT IN AN
AREA WITH GOOD AIR FLOW TO AVOID INJURY.
(k) Install the new o-ring [7] with engine oil, D00599 [CP2442] on the plug [4].
WARNING
ENGINE OIL IS POISONOUS. USE PROTECTION EQUIPMENT IN AN
AREA WITH GOOD AIR FLOW TO AVOID INJURY.
(l) Install the plug [4] with engine oil, D00599 [CP2442] into the oil nozzle [8].
(m) Attach the oil nozzle [8] to the TGB housing with the bolt [3].
1) Torque the bolt [3] to 95 in-lb (11 N·m) - 105 in-lb (12 N·m).

SUBTASK 72-62-00-020-001-F00
(1) Do these steps to disconnect the top-mounted connections from the TGB (Figure 401):
 ALL PRE SB CFM56-7B-72-0133

 ALL

(c) Disconnect the TGB tubes as follows:
1) Disconnect the oil supply tube [6] from the TGB [11].

nipple square flange [30].

(c) Put blanking plugs and caps on the openings.
SUBTASK 72-62-00-480-001-F00

 ALL

(4) Do these steps to disconnect the TGB [11] from the AGB [1]:

(c) Lubricate the horizontal drive shaft housing [5] with oil, D00599 [CP2442].

WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENTS OF THE OIL SYSTEM IF THE
ENGINE IS HOT. THESE COMPONENTS STAY HOTTER THAN OTHER
COMPONENTS. HOT COMPONENTS CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT OPEN THE OIL SYSTEM UNTIL THE PRESSURE GOES TO
ZERO. THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES
AFTER AN ENGINE IS STOPPED. A PRESSURIZED OIL SYSTEM CAN
RELEASE A SPRAY OF HOT OIL THAT CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON YOU. PUT ON CLOTHES, GOGGLES,
AND OTHER EQUIPMENT FOR PROTECTION, OR LET THE ENGINE
BECOME COOL. HOT OIL CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT LET OIL STAY ON YOUR SKIN. YOU CAN ABSORB
POISONOUS MATERIALS FROM THE OIL THROUGH YOUR SKIN.
CAUTION
DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON THE ENGINE OR OTHER
COMPONENTS. IMMEDIATELY CLEAN THE COMPONENT IF OIL FALLS
ON IT. OIL CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO PAINT AND RUBBER.
CAUTION
DO NOT LET ALKALINE CLEANING FLUID GET IN THE ENGINE OIL.
VERY SMALL QUANTITIES OF THIS FLUID CAN CHEMICALLY CHANGE

(e) Move the TGB sleeve [4] rearward on the horizontal drive shaft housing [5] to get access

WARNING
DO NOT LET OIL STAY ON YOUR SKIN. YOU CAN ABSORB POISONOUS
MATERIALS FROM THE OIL THROUGH YOUR SKIN.
CAUTION
DO NOT LET ALKALINE CLEANING FLUID GET IN THE ENGINE OIL. VERY
SMALL QUANTITIES OF THIS FLUID CAN CHEMICALLY CHANGE THE OIL.
THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE.
(1) Do these steps to prepare the TGB for the installation:
(a) Lubricate a new O-ring [27] with oil, D00599 [CP2442] and install it in the sleeve groove
(Figure 402).
(b) Lubricate a new O-ring [31] with oil, D00599 [CP2442] and install it in the groove of the
adaptor [32] (Figure 401).
(c) Lubricate the horizontal drive shaft housing [5] with oil, D00599 [CP2442].
(d) Fully retract the TGB sleeve [4] on the horizontal drive shaft housing [5] and the
horizontal drive shaft [26] in the TGB [11].
(e) Lubricate the radial drive shaft splines with oil, D00599 [CP2442] (Figure 401).
(f) Lubricate the threads of the bolts [8] and the bolts [17] that attach the TGB [11] to the
engine with graphite mineral vaseline, D00601 [CP2101].
(g) Make sure that the ring on the TGB [11] is serviceable (View A-A).
(h) Make sure that the gasket [16] of the oil return tube is serviceable.
SUBTASK 72-62-00-420-009-F00
(2) Install the outer radial drive shaft into the fan frame strut.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 72-62-00-420-002-F00
(3) Do these steps to install the TGB [11] (Figure 401):
CAUTION
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU ENGAGE THE OUTER RADIAL DRIVE SHAFT
WITH THE INPUT BEVEL GEAR OF THE TGB. IF YOU ARE NOT
CAREFUL, DAMAGE TO THE SEALS AND SPLINES COULD OCCUR.
(a) Engage horizontally the outer radial drive shaft splines in the input bevel gear of the
TGB [11]; put the TGB [11] in its position on the fan frame.
(b) While you hold the TGB [11] in its position, install the top two bolts [8], washers [9], and
the nuts [10] that attach the TGB [11] to the fan frame.
1) Tighten the nuts [10] but do not apply the final torque.
(c) Install the bottom bolts [17], washers [18], and the nuts [19] that attach the TGB [11] to
the fan frame.
1) Tighten the nuts [19] but do not apply the final torque.
SUBTASK 72-62-00-420-003-F00
(4) Engage the horizontal drive shaft [26] as follows (Figure 402):
(a) Lubricate the splines on the horizontal drive shaft with oil, D00599 [CP2442].
(b) Move the horizontal drive shaft [26] forward and carefully engage it in the AGB input gear.
1) If the splines do not align, handcrank the AGB to match and engage the horizontal
drive shaft splines with the AGB gear splines.
a) Remove the locking cover of the locking adapter to turn the AGB geartrain.
(c) Lubricate the threads of the AGB [1] input gear with oil, D00599 [CP2442].
(d) Install the locking nut [25] on the AGB input gear.
NOTE: The locking nut has left-hand threads.
1) Tighten the locking nut [25] with your hand.
(e) If you removed the locking cover from the locking adapter, re-install the locking cover
before you do the subsequent step.
(f) Torque the nuts [10] and nuts [19] that attach the TGB [11] to the fan frame to 176 in-lb
(19.9 N·m) - 195 in-lb (22.0 N·m).
(g) Torque the locking nut [25] of the horizontal drive shaft [26] to 1330 in-lb (150.3 N·m) -
1590 in-lb (179.6 N·m).
1) Use the wrench, SPL-2192.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE RETAINING RING IS IN ITS CORRECT
POSITION. IF THE RETAINING RING IS NOT IN ITS CORRECT
POSITION, THE HORIZONTAL DRIVE SHAFT COULD DISENGAGE AND
CAUSE AN ENGINE FLAME OUT.
(h) Use a mirror to look through the three visualization holes to make sure that the retaining
ring is in its position in the locking nut groove.
SUBTASK 72-62-00-420-004-F00
(5) Install the TGB sleeve [4] as follows (Figure 402):
(a) Move the TGB sleeve [4] forward to its position on the AGB [1].
(b) Install the V-clamp [2].

72-62-00-200-802-F00Transfer Gearbox Internal InspectionPDF p. 1383
3. Transfer Gearbox Internal Inspection
A. General
(1) This inspection use a borescope to examine the internal surfaces of the Transfer Gearbox
(TGB).
(2) If you find the metal bearing particles in the magnetic chips detectors, do the internal
inspection. The borescope equipment will permit you to see if the rollers bearing for the input
or output bevel gear is damaged.

E. Procedure
WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENTS OF THE OIL SYSTEM IF THE ENGINE
IS HOT. THESE COMPONENTS STAY HOTTER THAN OTHER
COMPONENTS. HOT COMPONENTS CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT OPEN THE OIL SYSTEM UNTIL THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO.
THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES AFTER AN
ENGINE STOPS. A PRESSURIZED OIL SYSTEM CAN RELEASE A SPRAY OF
HOT OIL THAT CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT LET OIL STAY ON YOUR SKIN. YOU CAN ABSORB POISONOUS
MATERIALS FROM THE OIL THROUGH YOUR SKIN.
CAUTION
DO NOT LET OIL GET ON THE ENGINE, OR OTHER COMPONENTS.
IMMEDIATELY CLEAN THE AREAS THAT OIL FALLS ON. OIL CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO PAINT AND RUBBER.
CAUTION
DO NOT LET ALKALINE CLEANING FLUIDS TOUCH THE OIL WHICH WILL
GO INTO THE ENGINE. VERY SMALL AMOUNTS OF ALKALINE CLEANING
FLUIDS WILL DAMAGE THE ENGINE OIL.
DO NOT PUT THE OIL THAT IS DRAINED FROM THE ENGINE BACK INTO
THE ENGINE.
SUBTASK 72-63-00-922-003-F00

WARNING
DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENTS OF THE OIL SYSTEM IF THE ENGINE
IS HOT. THESE COMPONENTS STAY HOTTER THAN OTHER
COMPONENTS. HOT COMPONENTS CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT OPEN THE OIL SYSTEM UNTIL THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO.
THE PRESSURE GOES TO ZERO APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES AFTER AN
ENGINE STOPS. A PRESSURIZED OIL SYSTEM CAN RELEASE A SPRAY OF
HOT OIL THAT CAN BURN YOU.
WARNING
DO NOT LET OIL STAY ON YOUR SKIN. YOU CAN ABSORB POISONOUS
MATERIALS FROM THE OIL THROUGH YOUR SKIN.
CAUTION
DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON THE ENGINE OR OTHER COMPONENTS.
IMMEDIATELY CLEAN THE COMPONENT IF OIL FALLS ON IT. OIL CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO PAINT AND RUBBER.
CAUTION
DO NOT LET ALKALINE CLEANING FLUIDS TOUCH THE OIL WHICH WILL
GO INTO THE ENGINE. VERY SMALL AMOUNTS OF ALKALINE CLEANING
FLUIDS WILL DAMAGE THE ENGINE OIL.
DO NOT PUT THE OIL THAT IS DRAINED FROM THE ENGINE BACK INTO
THE ENGINE.

G. Accessory Gearbox Installation
SUBTASK 72-63-00-922-002-F00
WARNING
DO NOT LET OIL STAY ON YOUR SKIN. YOU CAN ABSORB POISONOUS
MATERIALS FROM THE OIL THROUGH YOUR SKIN.
CAUTION
DO NOT LET HOT OIL GET ON THE ENGINE OR OTHER COMPONENTS.
IMMEDIATELY CLEAN THE COMPONENT IF OIL FALLS ON IT. OIL CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO PAINT AND RUBBER.
CAUTION
DO NOT LET ALKALINE CLEANING FLUIDS TOUCH THE OIL WHICH WILL
GO INTO THE ENGINE. VERY SMALL AMOUNTS OF ALKALINE CLEANING
FLUIDS WILL DAMAGE THE ENGINE OIL.
DO NOT PUT THE OIL THAT IS DRAINED FROM THE ENGINE BACK INTO
THE ENGINE.
(1) Obey the above warnings and cautions throughout this procedure.
(a) For the references, obey the warnings and cautions in those tasks.

of the tool.
2) Attach a hoist to the 3-leg sling.
3) Apply a slight tension to the hoist.

(3) Do these steps to install the AGB on the engine (Figure 404):
(a) Install the AGB [1] on the accessory gearbox cradle, SPL-9145 as follows:
1) Set the AGB [1] on the cradle with the cradle support.
2) Slowly lower the AGB [1] onto the cradle support.
3) Engage the two end lock pins of the tool which hold the cradle support to the AGB.
4) Install the third lock pin in the AGB. Adjust the yoke with the screw.
5) Set the adjustment rack of the cradle support to position 4 and attach a hoist to the
support shackle.
(b) Remove the covers and caps from all drive pads and equipment holes of the AGB.
(c) Apply a slight tension to the hoist.
(d) Remove the AGB and the cradle support assembly from the cradle mount support.
(e) Install the AGB and the cradle support assembly on the engine (Figure 405 and
Figure 401).
1) Align the upper and lower clevis mounts on the AGB and fan case.

6) Install the straight pin [46] at the upper clevis mount.

(g) For the correct alignment of the AGB, make sure that you have these dimensions:
1) Dimension (DIM. B) = Dimension (DIM. A) +/- 0.002 in. (0.05 mm).
2) If not, adjust the dimensions (DIM. A) and (DIM. B) as follows:
a) Cut the lockwire or the cable which safety the nuts of the axial links ends.
b) Loosen the nuts of the axial link ends.
c) Turn the link rod.
d) Measure the dimensions (DIM. A) and (DIM. B) again.
<1> Make sure that the dimensions are correct.
<2> If it is necessary, adjust the dimensions again.
<3> If the dimensions are correct, continue to the next step.
e) Hold the link rod in position and tighten the nuts.
f) Torque the nuts to 675 in-lb (76 N·m)-745 in-lb (84 N·m).
(h) Make sure that the dimensions (DIM. A) and (DIM. B) are not changed.
1) If it is necessary, do the steps to adjust and measure the dimensions again.

NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) This is a visual inspection of the Accessory Gear Box (AGB) housing, clevis mounts, mount
links, turnbuckle, and lockwire.
B. References

D. Procedure
SUBTASK 72-63-00-010-001-F00
(1) Do this task: Open the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-010-801-F00.
SUBTASK 72-63-00-210-001-F00
(2) If you find damage that is more than the limits, replace the AGB, unless you are given other
instructions.
(a) These are the tasks: Accessory Gearbox Removal, TASK 72-63-00-000-804-F00,
Accessory Gearbox Installation, TASK 72-63-00-400-804-F00.
SUBTASK 72-63-00-210-006-F00
(3) Visually examine the mount fittings on the fan frame (Figure 601, Sheet 3):
(a) Cracks that extend from the bolt holes in the mount lugs
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Not serviceable.
2) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles is permitted for one crack that goes through
one mounting lug bolt hole, not more than 0.25 inch (6.35 mm) in length.
(b) Cracks in the areas of the mount lugs
1) Not serviceable.
2) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles is permitted for one crack 0.25 in.
(6.35 mm) in length.
(c) Nicks, marks, and scratches
1) There is no limit to the number of nicks, marks, and scratches which are permitted
with these conditions:
a) Not more than 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) in length.
b) Not more than 0.02 in. (0.51 mm) in depth, after you remove the high metal
(Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00).
c) Minimum separation of 1.0 in. (25.4 mm) between areas of damage.
SUBTASK 72-63-00-210-002-F00
(4) Examine the AGB housing for damage:
NOTE: If you find AGB displacement while working on any of the AGB mounted equipment, it
is recommended to do an inspection of the AGB mounts and rod links within the next
200 hours or 100 cycles.
(a) If you find AGB displacement when you do work on the AGB mount equipment, do this
step:
1) It is recommended to do an inspection of the AGB mounts and rod links in the
subsequent 200 hours or 100 cycles.
(b) Cracks
1) Not serviceable.
(c) Nicks, dents, or scratches
1) All damage is permitted with this limit:
a) Not more than 0.035 in. (0.89 mm) in depth after you remove the high metal
(Hand Blending - Maintenance Practices, TASK 70-10-07-800-801-F00).
SUBTASK 72-63-00-210-003-F00
(5) Examine the AGB clevis mounts for damage:
(a) Cracks
1) Not serviceable.
(b) Loose bushing in the clevis mounts
1) Not permitted.
(c) Loose mount pin
1) Not permitted.
a) Tighten the mount pin if it is necessary.
(d) Cracks or crazing in the AGB mount rubber are permitted.
(e) Eccentricity of the mounting pin axis relative to the axis of the outer bushing of the rubber
damper
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Maximum Serviceable Limit: Maximum allowed eccentricity (half of the difference
between the minimum and maximum clearances) is 0.06 in. (1.5 mm) (Figure 601,
Sheet 4).
2) A Continue-In-Service limit of 10 cycles or 25 hours is permitted to replace the
dampers (Replacement of a Damper in the Mount Fitting,
TASK 72-63-00-300-801-F00), if there is no contact of metal against metal.
SUBTASK 72-63-00-210-005-F00
(6) Examine the AGB upper and lower mount links, turnbuckle, and associated clevis for damage
(Figure 602):
(a) Axial and/or radial looseness of mount link or turnbuckle
1) Any amount is permitted if there is no contact between the mount links or turnbuckle
extremity and associated clevis.
CAUTION
THE MOUNT LINKS OR TURNBUCKLES SURFACES MUST BE
PARALLEL AS FAR AS POSSIBLE TO THE CLEVIS SURFACES
DURING THE CLEARANCE CHECK. DO NOT ROTATE THE ROD
LINK OR TURNBUCKLE. THE CLEARANCE CHECK MUST BE DONE
AT THE EXTREMITY OF THE LINKS. AN INCORRECT CHECK CAN
LEAD TO EQUIPMENT DAMAGE.
2) If a mount link or turnbuckle extremity is in contact with the AGB or engine clevis, a
maximum In-Service extension of 500 operating cycles is permitted before you do
the installation of a damper.
NOTE: On engine POST CFM56-7B-SB 72-0465, you already have a damper at
each link end.
a) Do these tasks for each link to replace the dampers:
<1> Axial Link End Dampers Removal, TASK 72-63-00-000-802-F00.
<2> Axial Link End Dampers Installation, TASK 72-63-00-400-802-F00.
b) For the AGB and engine clevis of the mount links:
<1> Impacts, marks, wear or fretting
<a> Any amount permitted if less than 0.008 in. (0.2 mm) in depth.
c) For the AGB upper and lower mount links, turnbuckle (if removed during
damper installation) (Figure 602, Sheet 2):
<1> Spherical bearing axial wear
<a> Dim. X = 0.1799 in. (4.57 mm) “max”.
<2> Spherical bearing radial wear
<a> Any amount.
<3> Ball groove and corrosion
<a> Any amount.
<4> External ring with missing lubricating lining
<a> Any amount.
<5> External ring tears
<a> Not serviceable.
<6> If you find damage that is more than the limits, replace the axial link
end(s) or the mount link.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
<a> These are the tasks: Axial Link End or Upper (Lower) Mount Link
Removal, TASK 72-63-00-000-803-F00 Axial Link End or Upper
(Lower) Mount Link Installation, TASK 72-63-00-400-803-F00.
NOTE: This task includes an adjustment of the AGB position.
SUBTASK 72-63-00-212-001-F00
(7) Examine the axial link ends dampers for damage (Figure 602):
NOTE: You must do this procedure only for engine POST CFM56-7B-SB 72-0465.
(a) Tears, cut
1) Any amount is permitted.
(b) Missing dampers straps
1) Any amount is permitted.
SUBTASK 72-63-00-210-004-F00
(8) Look for damage to the lockwire:
(a) Broken, missing or loose lockwire
1) Not permitted.
a) Do this task: Lockwire Installation, TASK 70-20-01-800-804-F00.
SUBTASK 72-63-00-410-001-F00
(9) Do this task: Close the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-410-801-F00.

G. Procedure
SUBTASK 72-63-00-000-001-F00
NOTE: You can do this repair if you can get access.
CAUTION
KEEP TRICHLOROETHYLENE, TRICHLOROETHANE, AND
PERCHLOROETHYLENE AWAY FROM TITANIUM PARTS. CHLORINATED
AND HALOGEN MATERIALS CAUSE DAMAGE TO TITANIUM PARTS.
(1) Remove the damper [1] with puller, SPL-18389. Refer to Figure 803.
SUBTASK 72-63-00-200-001-F00
(2) Do a check of the surface condition of the inner diameter of the mount fitting.
SUBTASK 72-63-00-120-001-F00
WARNING
METAL PARTICLES FROM MACHINING CAN CAUSE DAMAGE, INJURY, OR
IRRITATION TO YOU. USE PERSONAL PROTECTION EQUIPMENT.
(3) If necessary, do a hand blending to remove scratch marks or pits with abrasive cloth, G51412
[CP2721]. Refer to TASK 70-41-11-350-009 (70-41-11, Hand Blending) CFM Standard
Practices Manual and to the limits that follow:
(a) Dia A. Refer to Figure 802.
• Minimum Finish Dimension = 1.73228 in. (44.0 mm)
• Maximum Finish Dimension = 1.73326 in. (44.025 mm)
SUBTASK 72-63-00-110-001-F00
(4) Do a locally swab etching of the repaired area (for titanium material). Refer to TASK
70-53-11-110-023 (70-53-11, Swab Etching) CFM Standard Practices Manual.
CFM56 ENGINES (CFM56-7)
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 72-63-00-200-002-F00
(5) Do a fluorescent penetrant inspection of the repaired area. Refer to TASK 70-32-23-230-012
(70-32- 23, Fluorescent Penetrant Inspection - Portable Post-Emuslifiable) CFM Standard
Practices Manual.
No indication is permitted.
NOTE: Indications with a maximum dimension of less than 0.012 in. (0.3 mm) are
non-interpretable as indications.
SUBTASK 72-63-00-400-001-F00
(6) Install a new damper [1] as follows. Refer to Figure 801.
WARNING
USE THERMAL GLOVES WHEN YOU MOVE OR TOUCH HOT OR COLD
PARTS. HOT OR COLD PARTS CAN CAUSE INJURY.
(a) Decrease the temperature of the damper to 14°F (-10°C) maximum.
(b) Put the damper in position in front of the mount fitting and align it with the center of the
mount fitting with a 0.787 in. (20.0 mm) diameter pin installed in the second damper.
(c) Install the damper in the mount fitting with a wooden mallet.
(d) Make sure that the flange of the damper is in contact with the mount fitting.
SUBTASK 72-63-00-200-003-F00
(7) Final visual inspection.
(a) Make sure that the flange of the damper touches the mount fitting.

[5].
